## 6.5: DEMOLITION CHARGES & MINES


Demolition charges and mines represent a different approach to explosive ordnance, emplaced weapons that wait for their moment rather than being deployed in direct combat. They require preparation but offer effects that thrown or fired weapons cannot achieve.


### DEMOLITION CHARGES


Demolition charges are high-explosive packages designed for specific purposes: breaching fortifications, destroying infrastructure, collapsing tunnels, or creating obstacles. They are not combat weapons in the traditional sense, they are tools for engineering problems that happen to involve massive explosions.

# CHAPTER 7: ARMOR SYSTEMS

*"Armor is a philosophy made manifest. Show me what a soldier wears into battle, and I will tell you what their commanders believe about war. House Joric wraps their troops in ceramite and faith, they believe in holding ground, in absorbing punishment, in outlasting the enemy through sheer stubborn endurance. House Valerius dresses their operatives in shadow and whispers, they believe the best armor is not being where the bullet lands. House Volkov bolts scrap metal to leather and calls it done, they believe that intimidation is worth more than protection, that an enemy who fears you has already half-surrendered. Every suit of armor tells a story. Make sure yours tells the story you want told."*

*Armorer-General Yusuf Okonkwo, House Joric Quartermaster Corps*


## INTRODUCTION: THE SECOND SKIN


In the void between stars, the margin between life and death is often measured in millimeters of composite material. A plasma bolt that would vaporize exposed flesh splashes harmlessly against reactive plating. A blade that would open arteries skitters across hardened weave. A bullet that would punch through a lung flattens against trauma plates and leaves only a bruise. Armor is the difference, not always, not against everything, but often enough to matter.

The post-Silence galaxy offers an extraordinary variety of protective equipment, from the simple padded jackets worn by frontier settlers to the walking fortresses that House Joric deploys against the most dangerous threats. This chapter catalogs that variety, providing complete statistics, tactical analysis, and cultural context for armor across all tiers of availability.

Understanding armor requires understanding several interconnected systems:

**Damage Thresholds (Major / Severe)** determine how hard a hit lands once it connects. Every armor lists two thresholds, Major and Severe (add your level to both). A hit that lands but falls below your Major Threshold marks 1 HP; at or above Major (below Severe) it marks 2 HP; at or above Severe it marks 3 HP; Overkill adds 1 HP more per full 10 points over Severe. Good armor raises both thresholds, so the same shot that staggers a civilian barely scuffs a hardened Voidwalker.

Your armor's **Armor Slots** are its active soak pool. Spend 1 Armor Slot to drop a hit one severity tier (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to no HP). This is the value weapon Features reduce when they "reduce

your Armor Slots," and follows the Corebook Armor Slot rules. Restore spent slots through Repair Armor during a Short Rest or Repair All Armor during a Long Rest; special gear may restore more.

**Improvement Capacity** is how many modifications a weapon or armor can accept (the Improvement system, Chapter 10): a permanent build resource for bolting on chrome, with each upgrade costing Improvement points. It is not a per-fight soak, and it is separate from your Armor Slots.

**Evasion** is set by your class and Agility, not by your armor. Armor never adds a flat bonus to Evasion: only specific armor Features adjust it (*Flexible* +1 Evasion; *Heavy* -1; *Very Heavy* and *Massive* -2). That is the only way a suit changes how hard you are to hit.

**Burden** represents the weight and encumbrance of the armor. Heavier armor provides more protection but limits mobility, reduces stealth, and may require rest to wear for extended periods.

**Properties** provide special capabilities beyond basic protection, environmental sealing, sensor integration, stealth features, and more.

This chapter is organized by armor weight class (Light, Medium, Heavy), followed by House-specific variants, powered armor systems, and a complete property glossary. Each entry includes full statistics, tactical recommendations, and notes on availability and cultural significance.


> **CATALOG NOTE:** Core armor remains canonical and available. This chapter adds distinct patterns rather than replacing similarly purposed Core armor. Flexible Mesh Armor and Patrol Armor intentionally use different names from Core Mesh Armor and Security Armor because their features and manufacturing roles differ.

## 7.1: ARMOR MECHANICS RECAP


Before examining specific armor types, let us review the mechanical systems that govern their function. These rules are drawn from the Veilfarers Core Rules; this section provides a consolidated reference.


### DAMAGE THRESHOLDS


Every armor lists two **Damage Thresholds**, **Major** and **Severe** (add your level to both). When an attack hits, compare the damage total to them and mark a fixed amount of HP by tier:

**Minor (below your Major Threshold):** mark **1 HP**. Any hit that connects and is not soaked away costs at least this much.

**Major (at or above Major, below Severe):** mark **2 HP**.

**Severe (at or above your Severe Threshold):** mark **3 HP**. Apply a Condition or other complication only when the attack, weapon Property, or environment feature explicitly states it.

**Overkill:** for every full **10 points** by which the damage total exceeds the Severe Threshold, mark **1 additional HP**: Severe plus 10 marks 4 HP, plus 20 marks 5, and so on. Rust & Steel does not replace this Core interval.

The *amount* of damage rolled sets the *severity* of the wound, not an HP-by-HP total: a 6-point hit and an 11-point hit hurt the same if both fall below Major. A hit marks no HP only when an Armor Slot soaks it away (see below).

**Example:**

*Kira wears Combat Armor (Major Threshold 8, Severe Threshold 16). She takes a hit dealing 10 damage. That is at or above her Major (8) but below her Severe (16): a Major hit, so she marks 2 HP. She could spend 1 Armor Slot to drop it to a Minor hit (1 HP) instead.*

*Later she takes a hit dealing 18 damage. That meets her Severe Threshold (16): a Severe hit, so she marks 3 HP. No knockback or Condition is added unless the attack prints one.*


### ARMOR SLOTS (SOAK)


Each suit of armor has an **Armor Slot pool**. Spend 1 Armor Slot to **drop a hit one severity tier** (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to no HP). This is the value weapon Features reduce when they “reduce your Armor Slots.” Restore spent slots through Repair Armor during a Short Rest or Repair All Armor during a Long Rest. When the pool is spent, only your thresholds protect you.


### IMPROVEMENT CAPACITY


Separately, each weapon and armor has an **Improvement Capacity**, the number of modifications it can accept (the Improvement system, Chapter 10). Each upgrade has an Improvement Cost; this is a permanent build resource for installing mods, not a per-fight soak. This terminology matches the Core Rules: **Armor Slots** are the expendable soak pool, while **Improvement Capacity** measures permanent room for modifications.


### EVASION AND ARMOR WEIGHT


Armor no longer grants a flat Evasion bonus. Your Evasion is set by your class and Agility; armor changes it only through weight tags, applied by the suit's Burden: light, flexible suits may carry *Flexible* (+1 Evasion); heavy suits carry *Heavy* (-1 Evasion); powered or siege-grade suits carry *Very Heavy* or *Massive* (-2 Evasion). That is the only way armor changes how hard you are to hit.

**Armor Slot Recovery:**

Armor Slots never reset merely because combat ends. Restore them by choosing **Repair Armor** during a Short Rest or **Repair All Armor** during a Long Rest, using the exact Core procedure and suitable tools.

**Armor Condition Track:**

If the table adopted the optional Condition Track in Chapter 2, marking the final Armor Slot may degrade the armor one step only when the hit or established fiction also supplies a degradation trigger. Use the same four states as every item: Functional, Worn, Glitchy, Broken.

### PROFICIENCY REQUIREMENTS

Class Technology Access controls armor training even at Common tier. Wearing armor above the class's listed access imposes Disadvantage on every Roll materially involving movement, including Agility, maneuvers, evasion, climbing, and piloting while worn. It does not remove Reactions, create a random malfunction, or add a second penalty. Integrated systems and properties outside the character's access cannot be operated until the relevant access is trained. Precursor armor may add a specifically printed story gate or exception.

### BURDEN


**Burden** uses the Core procedure. **Burden Capacity = 6 + Strength modifier.** At capacity or below there is no penalty. At 1-2 Burden above capacity, movement is limited to one band per Spotlight and Agility or Strength Rolls made to run, climb, jump, swim, or resist forced movement have Disadvantage. At 3 or more above capacity, the character cannot move or take a physical Action while carrying the excess; at the start of their Spotlight they may drop any carried, non-secured items as a free effect until the excess is lower. Armor Burden always counts while worn.

Armor Burden values typically range from 1 (light armor) to 4+ (heavy powered armor). This Burden is always counted while the armor is worn, you cannot "drop" armor the way you might drop a heavy weapon.


### DONNING AND DOFFING


Putting on or removing armor takes time:


| ARMOR TYPE | DON TIME | DOFF TIME |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Light Armor** | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| **Medium Armor** | 5 minutes | 2 minutes |
| **Heavy Armor** | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| **Powered Armor** | 5 minutes (with assistance) or 15 minutes (solo) | 3 minutes (with assistance) or 10 minutes (solo) |


**Emergency Doffing:** Most armor includes quick-release mechanisms for emergency removal. Emergency doffing takes 1 Action but renders the armor temporarily unwearable (requires 10 minutes to reset the releases).


## 7.2: LIGHT ARMOR


Light armor prioritizes mobility over protection. It offers modest defensive benefits while imposing minimal penalties on movement, stealth, and agility. Light armor is the choice of scouts, infiltrators, and anyone who relies on not being hit rather than surviving hits.


### DESIGN PHILOSOPHY


Light armor accepts a fundamental trade-off: you will be easier to hurt if you are hit, but you will be hit less often because you can move freely, react quickly, and take advantage of cover and concealment that heavier armor would prevent.

This philosophy suits certain tactical approaches:

- **Mobility-focused combat:** Characters who rely on repositioning, flanking, and hit-and-run tactics

- **Stealth operations:** Characters who need to move silently and avoid detection

- **Social situations:** Characters who need protection that doesn't advertise itself

- **Extended operations:** Characters who need to wear armor for days without fatigue

Light armor is not appropriate for:

- Front-line combat against serious opposition

- Holding positions under sustained fire

- Situations where being hit is inevitable

## 7.3: MEDIUM ARMOR


Medium armor represents the balance point between protection and mobility. It provides meaningful defense against military weapons while still allowing reasonable freedom of movement. Medium armor is the standard choice for professional soldiers, security personnel, and anyone who expects serious combat.


### DESIGN PHILOSOPHY


Medium armor accepts that its wearer will be in the fight, not avoiding combat through stealth, not relying on overwhelming firepower to end engagements quickly, but engaging enemies in sustained exchanges where both sides will take hits. The armor must be good enough to survive those hits while not being so heavy that it prevents tactical movement.

This philosophy suits:

- **Front-line infantry:** Soldiers who need protection for the duration of an engagement

- **Security personnel:** Guards and responders who face varied threats

- **Mercenaries:** Professional combatants who need reliable, maintainable protection

- **Hostile environment operators:** Personnel who need combat capability in dangerous conditions

Medium armor is not appropriate for:

- Deep infiltration or stealth operations

- High-society social situations

- Extended wear without support infrastructure

## 7.4: HEAVY ARMOR


Heavy armor prioritizes protection above all other considerations. It offers the highest damage resistance, the most Armor Slots, and often additional systems that lighter armors cannot support. In exchange, it imposes significant mobility penalties and requires substantial investment in Strength or servo-assistance.


### DESIGN PHILOSOPHY


Heavy armor assumes that you will be hit, repeatedly, by powerful weapons, and you need to survive it. The wearer accepts limited mobility, increased fatigue, and reduced agility in exchange for the ability to walk through

fire that would kill anyone else. Heavy armor turns its wearer into a walking fortress.

This philosophy suits:

- **Assault specialists:** Troops whose job is to breach fortified positions

- **Heavy weapons operators:** Personnel who stand and deliver sustained firepower

- **Point defense:** Individuals who must hold a position against all attacks

- **Vehicle crew:** Personnel who can rely on vehicles for mobility

Heavy armor is not appropriate for:

- Mobile warfare requiring rapid repositioning

- Stealth or infiltration of any kind

- Operations requiring extended foot movement


- Situations without logistical support

## 7.5: HOUSE-SPECIFIC ARMOR


Each Great House has developed distinctive armor traditions reflecting their philosophy, aesthetics, and tactical doctrine. House-specific armor offers unique properties not available in generic designs, but it also carries the weight of that House's identity.


### HOUSE SOLARI: THE GILDED CAGE SERIES


*"Beauty is armor. Elegance is defense. Let them see you coming, let them see your glory, and let their hands tremble on their weapons."*

House Solari approaches armor as they approach everything: as an art form that happens to serve a practical purpose. Their armor is beautiful, often

dramatically so, incorporating flowing lines, brilliant colors, and reflective surfaces that catch the light. But beneath the aesthetics, Solari armor is precisely engineered, the beauty is the first layer of defense, and more conventional protection lies beneath.

**Availability:** House Solari suppliers, exclusive clothiers serving the nobility. Wearing Solari armor without Solari affiliation may cause diplomatic complications.

### HOUSE KUROGANE: THE INTEGRATOR SERIES


*"The flesh is the platform. The machine is the upgrade. The armor is the interface."*

House Kurogane designs armor as part of an integrated system with cybernetic augmentation. Their philosophy holds that the distinction between worn equipment and integrated equipment is artificial, both should work together as a unified platform. Kurogane

armor interfaces directly with the wearer's augmentations, enhancing both.

**[NEW] System Override Property:** Once per Long Rest as a Reaction when a printed effect would take one installed augmentation offline, cancel that shutdown. Damage, Conditions, costs, and every other part of the triggering effect still resolve.

**[NEW] Distributed Processing Property:** The armor's computational systems can assist with mental tasks. +2 to Knowledge Rolls involving analysis, calculation, or data processing.

**Description:** The Integration Platform is the pinnacle of Kurogane's armor philosophy, not so much a suit as a second body, designed to work in perfect harmony with extensive cybernetic modification. Wearers report that the boundary between their augmentations and the armor becomes unclear; everything is one system, one self, one optimized whole.

**Availability:** House Kurogane exclusive. Requires extensive augmentation and Kurogane affiliation.

cobbled together from salvage, but it works. The aesthetics of violence are their own kind of beauty.

## 7.6: POWERED ARMOR & EXOSKELETONS


Powered armor represents the fusion of personal armor with mechanical enhancement, servo-assisted systems that amplify the wearer's capabilities while providing

protection beyond what passive armor can offer. These systems blur the line between armored infantry and light vehicles.


### POWER ARMOR CLASSIFICATION


**Exoskeletons:** External frame systems worn over conventional clothing or light armor. They provide Strength enhancement and load-bearing capability but limited protection. Exoskeletons are used primarily for industrial purposes (heavy lifting, construction) but have military applications.

**Light Powered Armor:** Form-fitting servo-assisted armor providing moderate protection with significant enhancement. Light powered armor maintains the wearer's mobility while adding strength and durability.

**Heavy Powered Armor:** Fully enclosed systems that transform the wearer into a walking weapons platform. Heavy powered armor provides vehicle-grade protection but requires significant training and support infrastructure.

**[NEW] Load-Bearing Property:** The exoskeleton includes mounting points for heavy equipment. Up to 6 Burden worth of equipment can be mounted on the frame, reducing effective Burden to 0 for carried items.

**Description:** The industrial exoskeleton is a tool, not a weapon, designed for dockworkers, construction personnel, and anyone who needs to move heavy loads without mechanical assistance. It's an open frame that

attaches at the legs, waist, and back, leaving the arms and upper body relatively unencumbered. The servo motors take the weight; the wearer just provides direction.

**Tactical Application:** Logistics, heavy equipment transport, and any situation requiring sustained heavy lifting. Can be repurposed for combat (heavy weapon operation, crew-served weapon transport) but provides minimal protection.

**Availability:** Industrial suppliers, ship chandleries, construction contractors. Legal everywhere; this is work equipment.

## 7.7: ARMOR PROPERTIES GLOSSARY


This section consolidates all armor properties introduced in this chapter for quick reference. Properties marked [NEW] are introduced in this expansion; properties marked [CR] are from the Core Rules.


### STANDARD PROPERTIES


**[NEW] Ablative (X):** Track X charges separately from Armor Slots. After severity is determined but before HP is marked, spend at most 1 charge to lower the hit one severity step. Repair All Armor restores all charges; the property never lowers maximum Armor Slots or reduces direct HP damage.

**[NEW] Augment-Sync:** After each Long Rest, choose one installed augmentation that grants a printed flat bonus to a Core Trait Roll; increase that one bonus by +1 while this armor is worn. If no augmentation grants such a bonus, this property has no effect. It never increases damage, Evasion, Thresholds, HP, Armor Slots, resources, dice, duration, or number of targets.

**[NEW] Augment-Sync (Enhanced):** Use Augment-Sync, but increase the chosen printed bonus by +2 instead of +1. Once per scene before a Roll that uses it, mark 1 Stress to gain Advantage on that Roll.

**[NEW] Modular Hardpoints (X):** The armor has X modification Hardpoints. Each installed armor modification consumes one Hardpoint and its listed Improvement Cost; no fictional bundling increases capacity.

**[NEW] Distributed Processing:** Gain +2 on Knowledge Rolls made for analysis, calculation, or data processing. It never modifies Spellcast Rolls, attack Rolls, Reaction Rolls, or Knowledge (Medicine) Rolls.

**[NEW] Blade-Sheaths:** The armor includes concealed storage for up to 4 small blades, drawable as a free effect.

**[NEW] Breaching Shield:** Once per round as a Reaction before an attack you can perceive is rolled against you, impose Disadvantage on that attack. You must have one hand free to brace the shield; there is no personal facing rule.

**[NEW] Climate-Controlled:** Ordinary hot or cold weather causes the wearer no Stress. This is comfort control, not sealed life support, and grants no Resistance or immunity to printed Fire, Cold, vacuum, radiation, toxic, or pressure damage.

**[NEW] Concealable Holster:** The armor includes a concealed holster for one small weapon.

**[NEW] Dazzling:** Once per scene as an Action, every other creature within Very Close range that can see the wearer makes an Agility Reaction Roll, DC 15; on failure it becomes Blinded until the end of its next Spotlight, on success nothing changes.

**[NEW] Diagnostic:** Gain Advantage on Knowledge (Medicine) Rolls made only to assess an injury; it grants no healing or repair bonus.

**[NEW] Displacement:** Attacks against the wearer from beyond Very Close range have Disadvantage. It creates no second miss roll after an attack hits.

**[CR] Environmental:** The armor is sealed against vacuum, hostile atmospheres, and environmental hazards. Includes life support.

**[NEW] Enhanced Senses:** The armor grants Advantage on Instinct Rolls to detect threats and permits attempts to detect Hidden creatures within Far range.

**[NEW] Flexible:** The armor does not restrict movement. No penalties to Agility Rolls, acrobatics, or similar physical activities.

**[NEW] Flight (Limited):** The armor includes anti-gravity or thruster systems for flight. 10 minutes continuous flight, then 1 hour recharge.

**[NEW] Reactive Plating:** Once per scene after severity is determined but before HP is marked, lower the hit one severity step without spending an Armor Slot. It cannot reduce direct HP damage or apply twice to one hit.

**[NEW] Hardened (Type):** Increase Major and Severe Thresholds by 2 against the canonical damage type in parentheses: Physical, Energy, Void, Neural, or All. Hardened is not Resistance and never halves damage.

**[NEW] Hazard-Sealed:** Immunity to contact or inhalation-based poisons, diseases, and radiation while sealed.

**[NEW] Identification Display:** The armor includes prominent, configurable identification panels.

**[NEW] Impact-Resistant:** Increase Major and Severe Thresholds by 2 against Physical damage carrying the Blunt or Impact tag. It does not halve damage.

**[NEW] Inspiring:** Allies within Very Close range gain +1 to Reaction Rolls against fear and morale effects.

**[NEW] Integrated Comms:** Built-in communication systems (10 km range or extended through relay).

**[NEW] Integrated Stun System:** It holds 6 charges, restored on a Long Rest with power. Spend an Action and 1 charge to make a melee attack; on a hit the target makes a Strength Reaction Roll, DC 15. On failure apply the Core Stunned condition and its normal clearing rule; on success no Condition is applied.

**[NEW] Integrated Weapon Mount(s) (X):** X hardpoints for mounting weapons. Mounted weapons don't count against Burden and can be fired without hands.

**[NEW] Intimidating:** +1 on Presence Rolls made for social interaction to threaten, coerce, or frighten while wearing visibly.

**[NEW] Jury-Rigged:** After the wearer resolves Failure with Fear on a Roll where the armor materially protected or assisted them, the armor degrades one step on the adopted Condition Track. If that module is inactive, reduce maximum Armor Slots by 1, minimum 0, until Repair All Armor. Matching dice remain a Critical Success. Knowledge (Tech) Rolls made during a rest to repair this armor have Advantage.

**[NEW] Last Stand:** Once per Long Rest, when reduced to 0 HP, enter Dying normally but immediately take one Action as a Reaction before the Dying prohibition on actions applies. This is not a Death Move, cannot restore the wearer's HP, and causes no automatic death. After it resolves, the character cannot act and begins normal Dying Progress on their next Spotlight.

**[NEW] Load-Bearing:** Mounting points for heavy equipment. Up to listed Burden worth of equipment can be mounted at 0 effective Burden.

**[NEW] Low-Profile:** The armor's visual signature is minimized. +1 to Agility Rolls to avoid detection vs. visual detection.

**[NEW] Magnetic:** Integrated mag-boots for walking on metal surfaces in zero-G and resisting knockback on metal surfaces.

**[NEW] Modular:** Standard attachment points for additional equipment. 3 Burden of equipment can be attached externally.

**[NEW] Phase-Step:** Once per scene at the start of your Spotlight, teleport to one visible, unoccupied point within Very Close range as a free effect. It cannot cross a barrier that blocks phasing.

**[NEW] Pocketed:** Numerous pouches and attachment points. Carry 2 additional small items without increasing Burden.

**[NEW] Power-Cell (X hours):** The armor requires power to operate active systems. Power cell lasts X hours.

**[NEW] Rage-Fueled:** While at 3 or more Stress, add +1 to melee damage totals. While Overwhelmed at maximum Stress, add +2 instead. It never changes current or maximum Armor Slots.

**[NEW] Sensor-Baffling:** Countermeasures against electronic detection. Sensor-based detection suffers Disadvantage.

**[NEW] Servo-Assisted:** Gain +1 on Strength Rolls made for lifting, carrying, climbing, or forced movement, increase Burden capacity by 1, and reduce the armor's effective Burden by 1. It never changes the Strength Trait, attacks, damage, or Reaction Rolls.


**[NEW] Servo-Assisted (Full):** Comprehensive servo systems. The wearer automatically meets Strength requirements imposed solely by the armor's weight; other Strength Rolls use the wearer's normal Trait.

**[NEW] Servo-Leap:** Enhanced jumping. Jump twice normal distance horizontally, three times normal height.

**[NEW] Silent:** Gain +2 on Agility Rolls to avoid auditory detection while moving. It grants no visual concealment and does not preserve Hidden after an aggressive Action.

**[NEW] Silent Running:** While the wearer moves no more than one range band during their Spotlight, the servos impose no penalty on Agility Rolls to avoid auditory detection.

**[NEW] Social:** The armor appears appropriate for social situations. Doesn't register as armor to casual observation.

**[NEW] Solar Absorption:** In established bright direct light, add +1 to Energy-weapon damage totals and the armor may use Dazzling twice per scene instead of once.

**[NEW] Specimen Containers:** Secure stasis-preserved containers for up to 4 small specimens.

**[NEW] Spiked:** At the end of each round, each enemy currently Grappling the wearer takes 1d4 Physical damage once through normal Thresholds and Armor Slots.

**[NEW] Strength Enhancement (X):** Gain +X on Strength Rolls made only to lift or carry and increase Burden capacity by X. It never changes the Strength Trait, attacks, damage, Evasion, Thresholds, or Reaction Rolls.

**[NEW] System Override:** Once per Long Rest as a Reaction when a printed effect would take one installed augmentation offline, cancel that shutdown. Every other part of the triggering effect resolves.

**[NEW] Terror:** Enemies within Very Close range take -1 to Reaction Rolls against fear and morale effects.

**[NEW] Thermoptic Camouflage:** Activate as an Action for up to 1 hour. Gain Advantage on Agility Rolls to avoid visual detection while stationary or after moving at most one band during the Spotlight. An aggressive Action ends it. Afterward it recharges for 10 minutes.

**[NEW] Thermoptic Camouflage (Advanced):** As Thermoptic Camouflage, but it lasts up to 4 hours and retains its Advantage after movement of up to two bands during the Spotlight. An aggressive Action still ends it.

**[NEW] Thruster Assist:** Move normally in zero-G and gain Advantage on Agility or Finesse Rolls made to maneuver there.

**[NEW] Thruster Pack:** Move normally in zero-G for up to 4 hours of maneuvering or 30 minutes of continuous thrust. In gravity, hover and move normally for at most 1 minute before landing; that minute counts against continuous thrust.

**[NEW] Uplink:** With a neural-interface augmentation, operate one owned compatible drone or personal device within Close range without using hands. It still costs the normal Action, Spotlight, Stress, and Roll; it grants no extra Action and cannot control a ship station remotely.

**[NEW] Weather-Proof:** Gain Advantage on Reaction Rolls against weather, temperature, corrosive rain, or airborne particulates, and increase Major and Severe Thresholds by 2 against their damage. It grants no immunity or vacuum protection.

# CHAPTER 8: AUGMENTATIONS & CYBERNETICS

*"The first cut is the hardest. Not physically, the surgeons handle that, and the anesthetics are excellent these days. The hardest part is the moment before, when you're lying on the table and you know that in a few hours, you won't be entirely human anymore. Something that was flesh will be metal. Something that was born will be built. You tell yourself it's just an upgrade, like getting a better weapon or a faster ship. But weapons and ships don't become part of you. They don't whisper in the back of your skull. They don't dream.*

*The second cut is easier. By then, you've made peace with what you're becoming. By the fifth or sixth, you barely notice. That's the danger, really. Not that the machines will reject you, but that you'll forget there was ever anything to reject."*

*Dr. Yuki Tanaka, "The Architecture of Self: Philosophical Implications of Human Augmentation"*


## INTRODUCTION: THE MARRIAGE OF FLESH AND MACHINE


Augmentation runs from simple sensory implants to full-body conversions that leave only the brain organic, and it is as much a cultural question as a technical one. The Great Houses split on it: House Kurogane leads the field and treats modification as progress; House Joric permits it for soldiers but discourages it among civilians; House Solari finds heavy modification vulgar unless artfully concealed; House Volkov cares only whether it makes you more dangerous. For a character, augmentation is opportunity bought at a price: decisive capabilities set against installation risk, social stigma, and the hard limit of Augment Capacity.

This chapter provides comprehensive rules for cybernetic augmentation:

**Augment Capacity** (established in Chapter 2) determines how many augments a character carries comfortably. This limit creates meaningful choices about which enhancements to prioritize.

**Augmentation Categories** organize the available options by function: Sensory, Neural, Physical, Combat, and Utility augmentations each serve different roles and suit different character concepts.

**The Augmentation Catalog** provides complete statistics for dozens of augmentations across all categories and tiers, from common implants available in any frontier clinic to experimental systems that push the boundaries of known science.

**House-Specific Augmentations** detail the unique technologies each Great House has developed, reflecting their philosophies and priorities.

**Living with Augmentation** addresses the narrative and practical implications of modification, how augmented characters interact with society, how they maintain their systems, and how modification shapes identity.


> **COMPLEXITY.** Complexity is a surgical rating from 1 to 4. Every augment costs exactly 1 point of Augment Capacity regardless of Complexity. Complexity modifies only installation difficulty and recovery time.

## 8.1: AUGMENT CAPACITY RECAP


Before examining specific augmentations, recall the limit that constrains them. The full rules are in Chapter 2 (and the Core Rules, Chapter 13); this is a condensed reference.


### AUGMENT CAPACITY


Your **Augment Capacity** is the number of augments your body carries comfortably. It equals the **sum of your three highest Trait modifiers** among Strength, Agility, Finesse, and Presence (minimum 0). **Humans and Synthetics add +2.**


### AUGMENT COST


Each augment installed costs **1 point of Augment Capacity**, whatever its power. **Complexity is not a Capacity cost:** retain the printed Complexity only to determine installation difficulty and recovery time.


### EXCEEDING YOUR CAPACITY


You are not hard-capped. Each augment installed beyond your Capacity costs **-1 to your maximum Stress** while it remains installed; the penalty is dynamic and lifts the moment your Capacity rises (raising a chosen Trait on level-up) or you have an augment removed. No ancestry takes a special modifier beyond the Human and Synthetic +2.


### OVERCLOCKING


In emergencies, characters can push past safe limits by **Overclocking**, redirecting stress through their augmentations. When Stress would exceed maximum:

- Convert each excess Stress to either 1 HP damage or 1 path resource spent - Hope if Awakened, Effort if Sleeping.

- Choose one installed augmentation to suffer 1 level of Degradation.

See Chapter 2 for complete Overclocking rules.


## 8.2: AUGMENTATION CATEGORIES


Augmentations are organized into five functional categories. Each category serves different purposes and appeals to different character concepts.


### SENSORY AUGMENTATIONS


Sensory augmentations enhance or replace biological senses, providing capabilities beyond natural limits. They are among the most common augmentations, the first step for many who eventually pursue more extensive modification.

**Common Applications:**

- Enhanced vision (low-light, thermal, magnification, recording)

- Enhanced hearing (extended range, filtering, recording)

- New senses (electromagnetic detection, chemical analysis, radiation sensing)

- Sensory filtering (flash protection, noise dampening)

**Character Concepts:** Scouts, investigators, snipers, security specialists, anyone who relies on information gathering.

**Typical Complexities:** 1-2 (sensory augmentations are generally minimally invasive)


### NEURAL AUGMENTATIONS


Neural augmentations interface with the brain and nervous system, enhancing cognitive capabilities or providing new modes of interaction with technology. They are more invasive than sensory augmentations and carry greater risks, but offer proportionally greater benefits.

**Common Applications:**

- Direct neural interface with computers and networks

- Enhanced memory (recording, indexing, recall)

- Accelerated cognition (faster processing, parallel thinking)

- Skill modules (downloadable expertise)

- Communication implants (silent speech, encrypted channels)

**Character Concepts:** Hackers, researchers, commanders, anyone who works with information or technology.

**Typical Complexities:** 2-3 (neural augmentations require significant biological integration)


### PHYSICAL AUGMENTATIONS


Physical augmentations enhance or replace biological systems related to strength, speed, and durability. They range from subtle enhancements to obvious mechanical replacements.

**Common Applications:**

- Limb replacement (arms, legs, hands with enhanced capabilities)

- Skeletal reinforcement (increased durability, weight bearing)

- Muscular enhancement (strength, speed, endurance)

- Organ replacement (enhanced lungs, hearts, livers)

- Subdermal armor (protective layers beneath the skin)

**Character Concepts:** Soldiers, laborers, athletes, anyone who relies on physical capability.

**Typical Complexities:** 2-4 (physical augmentations often involve significant biological displacement)


### COMBAT AUGMENTATIONS


Combat augmentations are designed specifically for warfare, integrated weapons, tactical systems, and enhancements optimized for violence. They blur the line between soldier and weapon.

**Common Applications:**

- Integrated weapons (concealed blades, built-in firearms)

- Targeting systems (aim assistance, trajectory calculation)

- Reflex enhancement (faster reactions, combat prediction)

- Defensive systems (personal shields, armor integration)

**Character Concepts:** Soldiers, assassins, bodyguards, anyone who expects to fight frequently.

**Typical Complexities:** 2-4 (combat augmentations often involve multiple integrated systems)


### UTILITY AUGMENTATIONS


Utility augmentations provide capabilities that don't fit neatly into other categories, tools, storage, environmental adaptation, and miscellaneous enhancements for specific purposes.

**Common Applications:**

- Tool integration (built-in equipment, specialized instruments)

- Storage (internal compartments, hidden spaces)

- Environmental adaptation (breathing, temperature, pressure)

- Medical systems (self-repair, drug delivery, vital monitoring)

**Character Concepts:** Engineers, medics, infiltrators, anyone with specialized professional needs.

**Typical Complexities:** 1-3 (varies widely based on complexity)

**Mechanical Benefit:** +4 to Knowledge Rolls. Once per scene, automatically succeed on one Knowledge task with DC 20 or lower; no dice are rolled and it generates no Hope, Effort, or Fear. Once per session, ask the Keeper one question about the logical implications of the current situation and receive a truthful answer based on available evidence.

**Description:** The superintelligence core represents the most advanced cognitive enhancement available, augmentation that pushes human intelligence beyond recognizable human limits. Users describe experiencing time differently; conversations feel slow, waiting feels interminable, and complex problems that would challenge unaugmented humans resolve themselves almost instantly. The psychological effects are significant; superintelligent individuals often struggle to relate to unaugmented humans and may experience profound isolation.

**Availability:** House Kurogane highest-level research assets. Extremely rare; possibly fewer than 100 individuals in the galaxy have this augmentation.

## 8.9: LIVING WITH AUGMENTATION


### SOCIAL IMPLICATIONS


Augmentation carries social weight that varies by culture, context, and visibility.

**In Core World Society:** Subtle augmentation is unremarkable, data-jacks, optical enhancement, and similar common modifications are expected among professionals. Visible mechanical modification draws more attention; some circles consider it gauche to display technological components that could be concealed. Extensive modification may be viewed with suspicion or distaste, particularly among the Solari-adjacent aristocracy.

**On the Frontier:** Augmentation is pragmatic, whatever helps you survive. There's less social judgment about visible modification and more interest in practical capability. However, some frontier communities are suspicious of the heavily augmented, associating extensive modification with corporate or House affiliation.

**In Religious Contexts:** Some traditions view augmentation as spiritual corruption, holding that the body is sacred and modification is desecration. Others see no conflict between faith and technology. The Sisterhood of the Void (associated with the Celestiari) takes a nuanced position, some augmentations are acceptable, others are not, and the distinction relates to whether the modification serves spiritual growth or material desire.


### MAINTENANCE AND MALFUNCTION


Augmentations require maintenance. Even the most reliable systems need periodic attention, cleaning, calibration, component replacement. Neglected augmentations degrade and eventually fail.

**Routine Maintenance:** Most augmentations require professional maintenance every 6-12 months. This is typically a brief outpatient procedure costing 10-25% of the augmentation's base price. Skipping maintenance risks malfunction.

**Malfunction:** Under the optional Condition Track, an augmentation degrades only through a printed trigger or when degradation was declared before a Roll and that Roll resolves Failure with Fear. A Glitchy augment goes offline on Failure with Fear while used; an Action and Knowledge (Tech), DC 15, restores it to Glitchy. A Broken augment requires professional repair. Without the Condition Track, neglect alone creates no Roll or malfunction.

**Repair:** Repairing a malfunctioning augmentation requires medical facilities and costs 25-50% of the

augmentation's base price. Field repairs are possible with appropriate skills (Knowledge Roll, DC 15) but are temporary; professional repair is still needed.


### IDENTITY AND AUGMENTATION


Extensive augmentation raises questions of identity that characters may grapple with. At what point does modification change who you are? If memories can be edited, what makes you the person you were? If your body is replaced, are you still human?

These questions don't have definitive answers, they're fodder for roleplaying and character development. Some characters embrace augmentation without concern, viewing it as simply tools. Others struggle with each modification, questioning what they're becoming. Both approaches (and everything between) are valid.

# CHAPTER 9: PERSONAL EQUIPMENT & GEAR

*"A gun is useless if you starve before you find something to shoot. Armor won't help if you freeze to death. The fancy ship means nothing if you can't patch the hull breach. Survival isn't about the biggest weapon or the heaviest armor, it's about having the right tool for the situation, maintaining it properly, and knowing how to use it when everything goes wrong. Weapons win fights. Equipment keeps you alive long enough to have fights worth winning."*

*Instructor Yeva Kortova, Free Fleet Survival School*


## INTRODUCTION: THE TOOLS OF SURVIVAL


Weapons and armor are only part of survival. This chapter covers everything else a crew needs in the post-Silence galaxy, where supply lines are thin and help may be weeks away: the tools that keep ships flying, the medicine that keeps bodies working, and the survival gear that turns a hostile world into a merely uncomfortable one. The prepared crew carries these things; the unprepared crew rarely lives to regret going without.

This chapter organizes personal equipment into functional categories:

**Survival Gear** covers equipment for hostile environments, life support, shelter, food and water procurement, and environmental protection beyond what armor provides.

**Medical Equipment** covers health maintenance and restoration, from basic first aid supplies to advanced surgical systems, along with pharmaceuticals and therapeutic devices.

**Tools and Technical Equipment** covers the instruments of repair, construction, and technical work, everything needed to keep equipment functioning and modify it for specific needs.

**Communications and Sensors** covers information gathering and transmission, scanners, communicators, and surveillance equipment.

**Security and Infiltration Gear** covers tools for bypassing obstacles, lockpicks, hacking devices, and other means of getting where you're not supposed to be.

**Personal Items and Miscellaneous** covers everything else, clothing, containers, lighting, and the small items that round out a character's kit.

Each category includes complete statistics, typical applications, and guidance on when specific items become essential rather than optional.


## 9.1: SURVIVAL GEAR


The galaxy contains countless ways to die that have nothing to do with violence. Vacuum, toxic atmospheres, extreme temperatures, radiation, starvation, dehydration, exposure, the universe is fundamentally hostile to human life, and survival beyond controlled environments requires appropriate equipment.

**Description:** A broad-spectrum antitoxin effective against most common poisons, chemical toxins, biological venoms, and many pharmaceutical overdoses. The antitoxin works by binding to toxin molecules and accelerating their breakdown.

**Effect:** Inject as an Action. The character gains Advantage on their next Strength Reaction Roll against any poison currently affecting them, and ongoing poison damage is halted for 10 minutes.

**Availability:** Medical suppliers.


### RADIATION TREATMENT


*Purge the poison from your cells.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 2 |
| **Burden** | 0 |
| **Uses** | 1 |
| **Cost** | 4 Credits |


**Description:** A treatment regimen (typically several injections over a few hours) that helps the body purge radiation damage and repair affected cells. The treatment is unpleasant, nausea, fatigue, and general malaise, but far better than the alternative.

**Effect:** Clear the Core Infected or Poisoned condition when its source has the Radiation tag and halt that source's ongoing damage. For the next 24 hours, Strength and Agility Rolls have Disadvantage. This exact modifier replaces any undefined Fatigued state.

**Availability:** Medical suppliers.


### REGENERATIVE ACCELERANT


*Heal faster, at a cost.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 3 |
| **Burden** | 0 |
| **Uses** | 1 |
| **Cost** | 9 Credits |


**Description:** A powerful healing drug that dramatically accelerates tissue regeneration. The

treatment is exhausting, the body's resources are consumed to fuel rapid healing, but results are impressive.

**Effect:** Inject as Action. Over the next hour, the character recovers 2d6 HP. However, they must consume food and water equivalent to a full day's rations during this time or suffer 2 Stress from metabolic exhaustion.

**Availability:** Military medical suppliers, high-end civilian medical facilities.


### MEDICAL DEVICES DIAGNOSTIC SCANNER


*Know what's wrong before you try to fix it.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 2 |
| **Burden** | 0.5 |
| **Cost** | 4 Credits |


**Description:** A handheld medical scanner that provides detailed information about a patient's condition, vital signs, injury assessment, toxicology, and basic imaging. The scanner doesn't treat anything; it tells you what needs treatment.

**Effect:** Using the scanner on a patient provides detailed information about their medical condition, including hidden injuries, diseases, and toxins. Grants +2 to Knowledge Rolls using medical training for diagnosis.

**Availability:** Medical suppliers.


### AUTO-DOC (PORTABLE)


*Surgery in a suitcase.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 3 |
| **Burden** | 4 |
| **Cost** | 9 Credits |


**Description:** A portable automated surgery system capable of performing complex medical procedures with minimal operator intervention. The auto-doc includes surgical manipulators, diagnostic systems, drug delivery, and a small supply of medical nanites. It requires a stable surface and approximately 30 minutes to set up.

**Effect:** Allows full surgical treatment in field conditions. Can treat conditions that would normally require a medical facility. The auto-doc has limited supplies for 5 major treatments before restocking (4 Credits). Operator still makes Knowledge Rolls using medical training, but gains advantage and can attempt procedures beyond their training (the DC moves up one rung).

**Availability:** Military and expedition medical suppliers.


### CRYOGENIC STASIS POD


*Stop time for the dying.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 4 |
| **Burden** | 10 (not portable by hand) |
| **Power** | External power required |
| **Cost** | 16 Credits |


**Description:** A full-body containment system that places the occupant in cryogenic suspension, near-absolute-zero temperatures that halt all biological processes. A patient in stasis does not age, does not worsen, and does not die, they simply wait until they can be revived at a proper medical facility.

**Effect:** A patient placed in stasis remains in exactly their current state indefinitely. Critical patients will not die while in stasis. Revival requires 1 hour and access to the stasis pod's controls. The pod requires external power; if power fails, the patient has approximately 12 hours of residual cooling before they begin to thaw.

**Availability:** Medical facilities, ship equipment suppliers.


### MEDICAL SERVICES


In addition to equipment, characters may need medical services from professionals.


### BASIC MEDICAL CARE


**Availability:** Any settlement with medical facilities

**Cost:** 1 Credit

**Effect:** Full recovery of all HP over 1 day of rest. Treatment of minor diseases and injuries.


### TRAUMA SURGERY


**Availability:** Medical facilities with surgical capability

**Cost:** 4 Credits

**Effect:** Treatment of severe injuries, restoration of lost HP, treatment of conditions requiring surgery. Recovery time: 1-7 days depending on severity.


### AUGMENTATION INSTALLATION


**Availability:** Qualified medical facilities (see Chapter 8)

**Cost:** Varies by augmentation

**Effect:** Installation of cybernetic augmentations. Recovery time varies.


### REGENERATIVE TREATMENT


**Availability:** Advanced medical facilities

**Cost:** 9 Credits

**Effect:** Regrowth of lost limbs or organs over 1-4 weeks. Requires specialized facilities.


### EXPERIMENTAL RESUSCITATION

**Availability:** House Kurogane specialized facilities only

**Cost:** 25 Credits

**Effect:** This service can treat only a character who is mechanically Final and has not died. With the patient in the facility, a specialist makes a Knowledge (Medicine) Roll, DC 20. On success, stabilize the patient at 1 HP and 3 Stress; on failure, the patient remains Final. It cannot revive a dead character, reverse a completed Death Move, or alter personality or memory without the player's consent.


## 9.3: TOOLS AND TECHNICAL EQUIPMENT


Technical equipment keeps ships flying, equipment functioning, and problems solved. In a galaxy where supply chains are unreliable and replacement parts may be weeks away, the ability to repair and maintain equipment is essential.


### BASIC TOOLS OMNI-TOOL


*The essential multi-purpose device.*


| STAT | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 1 |
| **Burden** | 0.5 |
| **Cost** | 1 Credit |


**Description:** The omni-tool is a standardized multi-function device combining numerous capabilities: communication, basic scanning, computation, flashlight, data storage, and interface port. Every spacer carries one; it's the baseline assumption for technological interaction in the Veilfarers galaxy.

**Features:**

- Short-range communication (10 km)

- Basic scanning (environmental sensors, simple analysis)

- Computation and data storage

- Integrated flashlight

- Universal interface port for connecting to systems

- Basic diagnostic capability for simple equipment

**Effect:** Having an omni-tool allows basic interaction with technology, communication with others, and simple repairs. It's required for many technical tasks and assumed for character competence.

**Availability:** Universal.


### TOOLKIT (BASIC)

| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 1 |
| **Burden** | 1 |
| **Cost** | 1 Credit |


**Description:** A set of mechanical tools for basic maintenance and repair, wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, diagnostic gauges, and similar hand tools. The kit allows work on most mechanical systems but lacks specialized equipment for advanced repairs.

**Effect:** Required for mechanical repairs. Allows maintenance and basic repairs on Tier 1-2 equipment. Repairs on higher-tier equipment require better tools.

**Availability:** Universal.

| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 2 |
| **Burden** | 2 |
| **Cost** | 4 Credits |


**Description:** A comprehensive toolkit including precision instruments, specialized tools, diagnostic equipment, and materials for complex repairs. The kit covers mechanical, electronic, and basic cybernetic work.

**Effect:** Allows repairs on equipment up to Tier 4. Grants +2 to repair checks. Includes spare parts for common repairs.

**Availability:** Technical suppliers.


### TOOLKIT (MASTER)

| --- | --- |
| **Tier** | 3 |
| **Burden** | 3 |
| **Cost** | 9 Credits |


**Description:** The finest available toolkit, including precision instruments, micro-manipulators, advanced diagnostics, and specialized equipment for virtually any technical task. The kit includes its own power supply and computational support for complex procedures.

**Effect:** Allows repair Rolls on equipment of any Tier and grants +4 on Knowledge (Tech) Rolls made to repair. A field repair that normally requires a workshop may be attempted at DC 25 if the necessary replacement part is present; success restores one degradation step or 1 Integrity, as applicable. The item must be named and feasibility fixed before the Roll.

**Availability:** High-end technical suppliers.

# CHAPTER 10: WEAPON & ARMOR MODIFICATIONS

*"Any fool can buy a weapon off the rack. It'll work, factory specifications guarantee that much. But factory specifications are designed for the average user in the average situation, and you're not average, and your situations certainly aren't. The weapon that fits your hand, compensates for your weaknesses, emphasizes your strengths, that weapon doesn't come from a factory. It comes from understanding what you need and having the skill to make it happen.*

*Modification is an art. It's also a risk. Every change you make is a deviation from tested, proven design. Get it right, and you have something unique, something that works better for you than anything mass-produced ever could. Get it wrong, and you have an expensive paperweight. Or worse, something that looks like it works until the moment it doesn't, and then you're dead because your gun jammed or your armor failed or your scope was half a degree off at exactly the wrong time.*

*So learn the craft. Understand the principles. Respect the risks. And when you're ready, make your equipment truly yours."*

*Master Armorer Chen Wei-Lin, House Kurogane Technical Academy*


## INTRODUCTION: THE ART OF CUSTOMIZATION


Mass-produced gear is built for the average user in the average situation, and you are rarely either. This chapter covers customizing weapons and armor to fit a specific person and a specific role, closing the gap between good enough for most people and perfect for this one.

This chapter provides comprehensive rules for customizing weapons and armor to meet specific needs:

**The Improvement System** governs how many modifications equipment can accept. Every weapon and armor piece has a limited number of hardpoints, attachment locations and system capacity for modifications. This limit prevents the creation of impossibly over-modified equipment while still allowing significant customization.

**Installation Rules** determine how modifications are attached. Some modifications are simple enough for field installation; others require professional workshops, specialized tools, or rare expertise. The installation check determines success or failure, and failure carries consequences.

**Weapon Modifications** enhance, alter, or specialize weapons for particular roles. From simple additions like extended magazines to complex overhauls like barrel replacements and firing mechanism upgrades, weapon modifications allow personalization of offensive capability.

**Armor Modifications** customize protective equipment for specific needs, enhanced environmental protection, integrated systems, specialized resistance, and improved performance in particular situations.

**Illegal Modifications** push equipment beyond legal limits or add capabilities forbidden by law. These Black Market options offer powerful advantages but carry legal risks and often technical dangers.

**Cosmetic Modifications** allow personalization that doesn't affect statistics but creates character, custom finishes, personal symbols, and aesthetic touches that make equipment uniquely yours.

Throughout this chapter, the underlying philosophy is balance: modifications should allow meaningful customization without breaking game balance, creating interesting choices rather than obvious optimal builds.


## 10.1: MODIFICATION RULES


### THE IMPROVEMENT SYSTEM


Every weapon and armor piece retains its canonical **Hardpoints** from the Core Rules: Hardpoints equal the item's Tech Tier. Rust and Steel also gives equipment an **Improvement Capacity**, a granular budget representing the combined complexity of installed modifications.

These restrictions coexist. Each installed modification consumes one Hardpoint and its listed Improvement Cost. Modifications share a Hardpoint only when a named **Shared Mount** rule explicitly permits that exact combination. A build is legal only when it fits both limits; fictional bundling never bypasses either budget.


### WEAPON IMPROVEMENT CAPACITY


Weapon improvement slot capacity is determined by weapon type and tier:


| WEAPON CATEGORY | BASE IMPROVEMENT CAPACITY |
| --- | --- |
| **Pistols** | 2 |
| **SMGs** | 3 |
| **Rifles (Assault, Battle, Hunting)** | 4 |
| **Shotguns** | 3 |
| **Sniper Rifles** | 4 |
| **Heavy Weapons** | 3 |
| **Melee Weapons (One-Handed)** | 2 |
| **Melee Weapons (Two-Handed)** | 3 |
| **Exotic Weapons** | Varies (see weapon entry) |


**Tier Modifier:** Higher-tier weapons are typically built with more sophisticated architecture that accepts modifications more readily:

- Tier 1-2: Base improvement slots as listed

- Tier 3: Base improvement slots +1

- Tier 4: Base improvement slots +2

- Tier 5 (Precursor): Special rules apply (see Chapter 18)

**Example:** A standard assault rifle (Tier 2) has 4 base improvement slots. A military-grade assault rifle (Tier 3) has 5 improvement slots. An experimental prototype assault rifle (Tier 4) has 6 improvement slots.


### ARMOR IMPROVEMENT CAPACITY


Armor improvement slot capacity is determined by armor weight class and tier:


| ARMOR CLASS | BASE IMPROVEMENT CAPACITY |
| --- | --- |
| **Light Armor** | 2 |
| **Medium Armor** | 4 |
| **Heavy Armor** | 6 |
| **Powered Armor (Light)** | 5 |
| **Powered Armor (Heavy)** | 8 |


**Tier Modifier:** As with weapons, higher-tier armor accepts more modifications:

- Tier 1-2: Base improvement slots as listed

- Tier 3: Base improvement slots +1

- Tier 4: Base improvement slots +2 **Example:** A standard combat shell (Medium Armor, Tier 2) has 4 improvement slots. An elite combat shell (Tier 3) has 5 improvement slots.


### MODIFICATION IMPROVEMENT COSTS


Each modification has a **Improvement Cost** representing how much of the equipment's capacity it consumes. Costs range from 0 (minor modifications that don't significantly impact capacity) to 3 or more (major overhauls that reshape the equipment's fundamental nature).


| IMPROVEMENT COST | MODIFICATION SCALE |
| --- | --- |
| **0** | Cosmetic or minimal (paint, grips, minor adjustments) |
| **1** | Standard modification (scopes, extended magazines, basic upgrades) |
| **2** | Significant modification (barrel replacements, integrated systems, major upgrades) |
| **3+** | Major overhaul (fundamental redesign, exotic systems, comprehensive enhancement) |


**Calculating Available Improvement Slots:**

Available Improvement Slots = Total Improvement Capacity - Sum of Installed Modification Costs

A weapon or armor piece cannot accept modifications whose total Improvement Cost exceeds its capacity. Attempting to over-modify equipment automatically fails.

**Example:** *Kira has an assault rifle with 4 improvement slots. She installs an extended magazine (1 improvement slot) and a reflex sight (1 improvement slot). She has 2 improvement slots remaining. She wants to add a suppressor (1 improvement slot) and an underbarrel grenade launcher (2 improvement slots), but their combined cost (3) exceeds her remaining capacity (2). She must choose one or the other.*


### INSTALLATION CHECKS

Installing a modification requires appropriate tools, adequate time, and a **Knowledge (Tech) Roll** when uncertainty and a meaningful consequence remain. Each entry's Installation DC is drawn from the Core ladder.

### INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS

Each modification states its required tools, time, and Installation DC. A value of **None** means a competent character can install it without a roll when the requirements are met.

### MAKING THE INSTALLATION ROLL

Superior tools, a professional workshop, detailed instructions, extra time, or long familiarity with the equipment grant Advantage when materially relevant. Inferior tools, rushing, an unfamiliar modification, or poor working conditions impose Disadvantage. Multiple sources do not stack; one of each cancels.

### INSTALLATION OUTCOMES

- **Critical Success:** The modification is installed, apply the normal critical payout, and choose one: halve the listed time or preserve one consumable component for later use.
- **Success with Hope:** The modification is installed; choose one: halve the listed time or learn one concrete future optimization for this item.
- **Success with Fear:** The modification is installed, but choose one consequence supported by the work: it takes twice the listed time, consumes one replacement component, or leaves a visible trace/warranty flag.
- **Failure with Hope:** It is not installed; materials remain reusable and the installer learns what tool, component, or preparation would permit a new attempt.
- **Failure with Fear:** It is not installed; the modification is damaged and unusable until repaired with Knowledge (Tech) DC 15. The base item remains usable unless the declared procedure required cutting into a core function, in which case that function is offline until the same repair. One roll causes at most one such result.

### WHEN A ROLL IS NOT REQUIRED

Do not roll for an entry marked None, for cosmetic work, or for a safe routine installation whose nominal DC is 10. A qualified professional with full facilities also completes a DC 15-or-lower installation automatically when no pressure or opposition exists. A player cannot roll a consequence-free task merely to fish for a Critical Success.

### REMOVING MODIFICATIONS


Modifications can be removed from equipment, freeing improvement slots for different modifications.


### STANDARD REMOVAL


Removing a modification requires:

- Appropriate tools (same as installation)

- Time (typically half the installation time)

- No check required for standard removal

The removed modification is intact and can be installed elsewhere (assuming compatibility).


### DIFFICULT REMOVAL


Some modifications are harder to remove:

- **Integrated Modifications:** Removal uses Knowledge (Tech) at the original Installation DC. Critical Success or either success removes it intact. Failure with Hope leaves it installed and intact. Failure with Fear leaves it installed and damages only the modification, which is unusable until repaired with Knowledge (Tech), DC 15, during a rest; the base item remains usable.

- **Damaged Equipment:** Repair the base item first. Attempting removal before repair uses Knowledge (Tech), DC 10: on success remove the modification intact; Failure with Hope leaves it installed; Failure with Fear leaves it installed and degrades the base item one step under the adopted Condition Track, or takes its core function offline until Knowledge (Tech), DC 15, restores it if the module is inactive.

- **Incompatible Removal:** An entry that requires specialist equipment cannot be rolled without it. Once the listed equipment is present, use the Integrated Modification procedure above; absence of equipment creates no Roll or hidden damage.


### MODIFICATION COMPATIBILITY


Not all modifications work with all equipment. Compatibility restrictions include:


### WEAPON COMPATIBILITY


**Weapon Type:** Some modifications only work with specific weapon types.

- *Example: A "Rifle Scope" only works on rifles, not pistols or melee weapons.*

**Firing Mechanism:** Some modifications require specific firing mechanisms.

- *Example: A "Burst Fire Conversion" only works on weapons that fire discrete projectiles, not beam weapons.*

**Physical Requirements:** Some modifications have physical requirements.

- *Example: An "Extended Barrel" requires a weapon with a replaceable barrel.*


### ARMOR COMPATIBILITY


**Armor Class:** Some modifications only work with specific armor weights.

- *Example: "Servo Enhancement" only works on Medium or Heavy armor with sufficient structure.*

**Existing Properties:** Some modifications require or conflict with existing properties.


- *Example: "Vacuum Seal Enhancement" requires the Environmental property; "Integrated Cooling" conflicts with thermal-signature mods.*

**Physical Space:** Some modifications require physical space that lighter armor lacks.

- *Example: "Integrated Medical System" requires Medium or heavier armor.*


### STACKING AND CONFLICTS STACKING MODIFICATIONS


In general, different modifications stack, their benefits combine.

- *Example: A weapon with both "Accuracy Enhancement (+1)" and "Targeting Laser (+1)" gains +2 to attack rolls.*

However, **identical modifications do not stack.** You cannot install the same modification twice on the same equipment.

- *Example: You cannot install two "Extended Magazines" on the same weapon.*


### MODIFICATION CONFLICTS


Some modifications conflict with each other, they cannot be installed on the same equipment simultaneously.

- **Physical Conflicts:** Modifications that occupy the same physical space.

- *Example: "Suppressor" and "Muzzle Brake" both attach to the barrel; only one can be installed.*

- **System Conflicts:** Modifications with incompatible systems.

- *Example: "Thermal Dampening" and "Heat Vent System" have conflicting heat management approaches.*

- **Property Conflicts:** Modifications that create contradictory properties.

- *Example: "Loud Enhancement" and "Suppressor" create opposite acoustic effects.*

Conflicts are noted in modification entries. Attempting to install conflicting modifications automatically fails.


### PROFESSIONAL INSTALLATION SERVICES


Characters without technical skills or appropriate tools can hire professionals to install modifications.


### PROFESSIONAL ARMORER


**Availability:** Most settlements with technical services

**Cost:** 25% of modification cost (minimum 1 Credit)

**Capability:** Can install any modification up to Tier 3 with no risk of failure (automatic success)

**Time:** Standard installation time


### MASTER ARMORER


**Availability:** Major settlements, House facilities

**Cost:** 50% of modification cost (minimum 2 Credits)

**Capability:** Can install any modification up to Tier 4; provides +2 to equipment performance for 1 month (fine-tuning bonus)

**Time:** Standard installation time or rushed (half time) with no penalty


### HOUSE TECHNICAL SPECIALIST


**Availability:** House facilities only

**Cost:** Varies (often requires House affiliation or significant payment)

**Capability:** Can install any modification including Experimental and House-specific; can attempt modifications that would normally be impossible

**Time:** As needed

## 10.3: ARMOR MODIFICATIONS


Armor modifications customize protective equipment for specific needs, enhanced environmental protection, integrated systems, specialized resistance, and improved performance in particular situations. Unlike weapon modifications that enhance offense, armor modifications expand defensive options and utility capabilities.


### PROTECTIVE ENHANCEMENTS


These modifications improve the armor's basic protective function.

| **Installation DC** | 15 |
| **Time** | 2 hours |
| **Compatible With** | Medium and Heavy armor |
| **Cost** | 4 Credits |


**Effect:** +1 to Major and Severe Damage Thresholds. +0.5 Burden.

**Description:** Additional armor plating installed over vital areas, heart, spine, throat. The extra protection adds weight but significantly improves survival against penetrating hits.

**Availability:** Military suppliers, quality armorers.

## 10.4: ILLEGAL MODIFICATIONS (BLACK MARKET)


Some modifications push equipment beyond legal limits, bypassing safety restrictions, adding forbidden capabilities, or incorporating technology too dangerous for civilian use. These Black Market modifications offer significant advantages but carry substantial risks: legal consequences if discovered, technical dangers from corner-cutting or unstable technology, and social stigma among those who recognize illegal hardware.


### LEGALITY AND RISK


**Legal Status:** Black Market modifications are illegal in most jurisdictions. Possession of illegally modified equipment typically results in confiscation, fines, and possible imprisonment. In strict jurisdictions (most Core Worlds, House territories during martial law), the penalties can include significant prison sentences or worse.

**Detection Risk:** Many illegal modifications are obvious to trained observers, modified firing mechanisms, concealed weapons, or equipment that simply shouldn't exist outside military arsenals. Others are more subtle but can be detected by detailed inspection (DC 15 to notice most illegal mods on casual inspection; DC 20 for well-concealed modifications).

**Technical Risk:** Black Market modifications often bypass safety systems, use unreliable components, or push equipment beyond design limits. They're more prone to malfunction than legal modifications, and failures can be dangerous.

**Heat Generation:** Acquiring and using Black Market modifications generates Heat (see Chapter 2). Simply purchasing generates +1 to +3 Heat depending on the modification's severity. Being caught with illegal modifications generates additional Heat.

**Risk:** The fixed discharge trigger is Failure with Fear on the overcharged attack Roll; no secondary die or die face creates it.

**Description:** A modification that bypasses safety limiters on energy weapons, allowing vastly increased power output. The modification is unstable; the power surge can cause the weapon's systems to fail catastrophically.

**Availability:** Black Market, desperate or reckless buyers.
