# CHAPTER 19: PRECURSOR HAZARDS & ANOMALIES

*"The Precursors didn't just leave artifacts. They left wounds in reality, places where the rules broke and never healed. Step wrong in a ruin, and you might find yourself three days ago, or made of crystal, or simply\... not. The treasures are real. So are the prices."*

*Expedition Report 447-Sigma, House Amaranth Archaeological Corps (Final Entry)*


## INTRODUCTION: WHEN REALITY BLEEDS


Precursor technology operated on principles that current science cannot explain. Their machines didn't follow the laws of physics, they rewrote them locally. And when those machines broke, or were abandoned, or simply stopped being maintained, the rewritten physics didn't always reset.

The result is **Anomalies**: persistent zones where reality operates according to rules the Precursors wrote and no one else can read. Time flows wrong. Space folds incorrectly. Cause and effect become suggestions rather than laws. These anomalies cluster in Precursor ruins but can occur anywhere their technology was used extensively, which, given how old the Precursors were and how widespread their civilization, means anywhere.

Anomalies cannot be fought with weapons. They cannot be negotiated with or bribed. They can only be survived, navigated, or avoided. This chapter provides rules for encountering anomalies, a catalog of common types, systems for generating Precursor ruins, and guidance on the complex economy of trading in artifacts.


## 19.1: ANOMALY MECHANICS


### DETECTING ANOMALIES


Anomalies are not always visible. Some manifest obviously, gravity reversing, time stuttering, crystals growing from nothing. Others are subtle until you're already inside them.

**Passive Detection:**

Characters with any of the following may notice anomalies before entering:

- Precursor Proficiency: Instinct Roll, DC 10 to sense an anomaly within Far range

- Veil-touched abilities: automatic awareness within Far range

- Specialized sensors: Knowledge (Tech) DC 15 to detect within Very Far range with proper equipment

- Celestiari empathy: May sense "wrongness" in affected areas

**Active Scanning:**

Characters can deliberately scan for anomalies:

- **Knowledge (Tech) DC 15:** Detect anomaly presence within Far range

- **Instinct (if applicable) DC 10:** Sense anomaly nature (what type it is)

- **Knowledge Roll, DC 15:** Understand anomaly parameters (boundaries, intensity, potential triggers)


### ANOMALY CLASSIFICATION


Anomalies are classified by **Tier** (danger level) and **Type** (nature of reality distortion).

**Tier Ratings:**


| TIER | DANGER LEVEL | EXAMPLE EFFECTS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | Minor | Inconvenient but rarely lethal. Strange but manageable. |
| **2** | Moderate | Can cause injury or trap characters. Requires careful navigation. |
| **3** | Severe | Can kill careless characters. May require specific solutions. |
| **4** | Extreme | Almost certainly lethal without preparation. May have no solution. |
| **5** | Catastrophic | Campaign-ending if encountered unprepared. Avoid at all costs. |


### NAVIGATING ANOMALIES


Most anomalies can be traversed, but doing so requires understanding their rules.

**Standard Navigation:**

Make one Action Roll with the Trait selected by the anomaly: Knowledge for temporal or reality-affecting phenomena; Agility for spatial distortion; Strength for gravitational force; Instinct for a biological anomaly. Veil knowledge may be a relevant Experience, never a seventh Trait.

| ANOMALY TIER | NAVIGATION DC |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 15 |
| 3 | 15 |
| 4 | 20 |
| 5 | 25 |

**Critical Success:** Navigate safely, learn one true operational fact about the anomaly, and resolve the normal Path payout.

**Success with Hope:** Navigate safely and resolve normal Path progress.

**Success with Fear:** Navigate safely, mark 1 Stress, and give the Keeper 1 Fear subject to the hard maximum of 12.

**Failure with Hope:** Remain at the entry and learn one viable adjustment that grants Advantage on the next navigation attempt.

**Failure with Fear:** Remain at the entry, mark 2 Stress, and give the Keeper 1 Fear subject to the hard maximum of 12. No character becomes trapped unless the entry defines a separate trigger and escape procedure.


### ANOMALY INTERACTION


Some anomalies can be affected by character actions:

**Stabilization:** With the equipment named by the entry, make a Knowledge Roll: Tier 1 DC 15, Tier 2-3 DC 20, Tier 4-5 DC 25. On success, suppress one named anomaly Feature for a number of hours equal to its Tier; Critical Success doubles that duration. Failure changes nothing. Failure with Fear also marks 1 Stress. Stabilization never closes the anomaly.

**Amplification:** No generic amplification Roll exists. An anomaly can be strengthened only by a complete entry or adventure rule that names the trigger, Roll, and changed effect.

**Closure:** Closure exists only when the entry names a viable method. After obtaining that method, start a visible six-segment Closure clock and use Knowledge at the Stabilization DC unless the entry names another Core Trait. Critical Success marks 2 segments; any other success marks 1; Failure with Hope marks none; Failure with Fear marks none and applies that entry's declared hazard. Filling the clock closes the anomaly. Void Scars explicitly cannot use this procedure.


## 19.2: ANOMALY CATALOG


### THE TIME-LOOP (TIER 3)


*"We've been here before. We've been here before. We've been here, "*

**Description:** A region (typically a room, corridor, or small structure) trapped in a repeating temporal cycle. Within the loop, events repeat endlessly, usually a 10-second to 10-minute span. Characters entering become part of the loop.

**Visual Signs:** Objects in slightly wrong positions. Dust patterns that don't match air currents. Faint afterimages trailing moving objects. A sense of déjà vu.

**Effects:**

- Characters inside the loop experience the same time period repeatedly

- Actions taken reset at the end of each cycle

- Memories persist between cycles (characters remember previous loops)

- Objects from outside cannot be permanently removed; they reset

- The loop continues until the **Anchor** is identified and addressed

**The Anchor:**

Every Time-Loop has an Anchor, the object, person, or event that caused the loop's formation. Common anchors include:

- A Precursor device that activated at the wrong moment

- A death that the universe is trying to "prevent"

- A paradox created by temporal manipulation

- An unfinished task that "needs" completion

**Navigation and Anchor procedure:** Finding the Anchor is a Knowledge Roll, DC 15. Success identifies it; Failure resets the current cycle with memories intact. Once identified, a second Knowledge Roll, DC 15, reveals one of three methods fixed when the loop is created: destroy the Anchor, complete its interrupted task, or accept its recorded outcome. Carrying out that method fills a visible three-segment Resolution clock: Critical Success marks 2, any other success marks 1, Failure with Hope marks none, and Failure with Fear resets the clock to 0 and marks 1 Stress. Filling it ends the loop. No result erases memories, removes a character from play, or creates a trapped state.

**Keeper Notes:**

Time-Loops make excellent puzzle encounters. The party has unlimited "attempts" but must figure out what the Anchor is and how to address it. Classic solutions include completing a task the original inhabitants couldn't, preventing a death that was trying to be prevented, or deliberately causing the event the loop was trying to avoid.


### THE CRYSTAL GROWTH (TIER 2)


*"It's beautiful. Like frozen lightning. Don't touch it. Don't touch anything it's touched."*

**Description:** A zone where crystalline structures are rapidly growing, consuming matter and converting it to crystal. The growth spreads from a central point, expanding outward at rates varying from centimeters per hour to meters per minute.

**Visual Signs:** Walls, floors, and objects coated in translucent crystal. Geometric patterns spreading across surfaces. Faint harmonic vibrations in the air. Sometimes, objects or creatures that have been fully crystallized, preserved in perfect detail but absolutely dead.

**Effects and crystallization:**

- The zone is Difficult Terrain: moving one band consumes the Action.
- A character entering active crystal or ending a Spotlight in contact with it takes 1d6 Physical damage, then makes a Strength Reaction Roll, DC 15.
- Track a visible three-segment Crystallization clock per exposed character. Failure marks 1 segment; Critical Success clears 2; any other success clears 1. Leaving the zone stops new Rolls but does not clear marked segments.
- At 1-2 segments, the character has Disadvantage on Agility and Finesse Rolls involving the crystallized limb. At 3, become Restrained and mark 1 direct HP at the end of each Spotlight until treated; at 0 HP use Dying and Final normally. Crystallization never declares death.
- Ten minutes of treatment outside the zone with tools and a Knowledge (Medicine) Roll, DC 15, clears 1 segment; Critical Success clears all. A Long Rest outside the zone clears all segments. Existing crystal is inert when the source is disabled.

**Navigation:** An Instinct Roll, DC 15, identifies a route that grants Advantage on the next movement or treatment Roll. A Knowledge Roll, DC 15, identifies the source.

**The Source:**

Crystal Growth originates from a Precursor device, usually damaged or malfunctioning. The device is converting ambient matter into a specific crystalline structure for unknown purposes. Destroying the device usually stops new growth but doesn't remove existing crystal.

**Keeper Notes:**

Crystal Growth creates urgency. Unlike Time-Loops, there's no infinite retry, the growth is spreading, and characters can die. Use it to force quick decisions and create tension around resource management (do we stop to search for treasure, or do we get out before we crystallize?).


### THE NULL-ZONE (TIER 4)


*"The silence is heavy. Not quiet, heavy. Like sound itself has weight here, and it's pressing down on everything."*

**Description:** A region where something fundamental has been removed from reality. Technology doesn't function. Energy doesn't flow. Light dims, sound muffles, and colors fade to grayscale. The Null-Zone is an absence made manifest.

**Visual Signs:** Colors desaturated toward gray. Shadows too deep. Lights dimming regardless of power source. An oppressive sense of weight or pressure. Absolute silence in the deepest areas.

**Effects:**

- **No Technology:** electronic, powered, and energy equipment is offline inside the zone. Purely mechanical gear functions. Items return online on leaving.
- **Muffled Sound:** Agility Rolls to avoid auditory detection have Advantage; speech carries only within Very Close range.
- **Dimmed Light:** unassisted visual detection beyond Close range is impossible.
- **Stress:** At the end of each minute, each exposed character marks 1 Stress. Before marking it, an Instinct Roll, DC 15, prevents that minute's Stress on success. At maximum use Overwhelmed normally.
- **No Veil:** Void, Psionic, and Veil-based Powers cannot be activated inside. Ongoing effects pause and resume only if their duration remains when the character leaves.

**Navigation:** Crossing is a Strength Roll, DC 15. Success crosses one band; Failure leaves the character in place. A Knowledge Roll, DC 15, identifies the suppression device if one is in the scene.

**The Nature:**

Null-Zones are believed to be areas where Precursor technology actively suppressed reality, perhaps for containment, perhaps for experimentation, perhaps as weapons. The suppression systems are long broken, but the suppression continues through momentum.

**Resolution:** A Null-Zone can use the universal Closure clock only after the crew reaches its suppression device and provides one Tier-4-or-higher power source. Merely waiting does not change it on campaign timescales.

**Keeper Notes:**

Null-Zones force players to rely on skills they might neglect, physical capabilities, mundane equipment, psychological resilience. They're excellent for "survival horror" encounters where the party's usual tools don't work.


### THE GRAVITY WELL (TIER 3)


*"Up is\... I don't know. I don't know where up is anymore."*

**Description:** A zone where gravity has become unstable, shifting direction randomly or creating multiple simultaneous gravity fields. Movement becomes a three-dimensional puzzle as "down" changes moment to moment.

**Visual Signs:** Objects floating at odd angles. Dust motes drifting sideways. Water pooling on walls or ceilings. Characters' hair and clothing behaving strangely.

**Effects:**

- **Shifting Gravity:** At the start of each round roll d8: 1-2 down, 3-4 up, 5 left, 6 right, 7 zero-G, 8 high-G. State the map orientation before the first roll.
- **Gravity change:** When the direction changes, every unanchored creature makes an Agility Reaction Roll, DC 15. On failure move one band in the new direction, take 1d8 Physical damage with the Impact tag if a solid surface stops that movement, and become Prone. On success reach the nearest safe surface without damage.
- **Movement:** In directional or zero-G states, use normal range-band movement. In high-G, movement is limited to one band per Spotlight. Ranged attacks have Disadvantage while gravity is not down; melee attacks use the normal attack procedure with no extra Roll.
- **Loose equipment:** Only an item deliberately dropped or already unattended moves one band with a gravity change. Carried gear never disappears by declaration.
- **Anchor:** Spend an Action and make a Strength Roll, DC 15, to anchor until you move; an anchored character ignores the next gravity-change Reaction.
- **Predict:** Spend an Action and make an Instinct Roll, DC 15. On success reveal the next gravity roll and gain Advantage on the next gravity-change Reaction.

**The Mechanism:**

Gravity Wells form around damaged gravity manipulation devices, usually Precursor environmental systems that regulated gravity on stations or ships. The device is still trying to function but has lost its calibration.

**Keeper Notes:**

Gravity Wells make standard tactics impossible. They're excellent for forcing creative problem-solving and creating memorable set-pieces. A combat in shifting gravity is something players won't forget.


### THE MIRROR BREACH (TIER 3)

*"That's me. That's exactly me. But I didn't raise my hand. Why is it raising its hand?"*

**Description:** Reflective surfaces show past, future, or parallel versions instead of faithful reflections. The boundary is obvious before anyone can trigger it.

**Crossing the zone:** A character who covers their eyes or avoids every reflective surface makes an Agility Roll, DC 15. Success crosses safely. On Failure with Hope, remain at the entry. On Failure with Fear, remain at the entry and become Dazed until the end of the next Spotlight.

**Looking into a reflection:** After more than ten seconds, make an Instinct Roll, DC 15. On success, learn one true visual detail about a nearby possible timeline. On Failure with Hope, learn nothing. On Failure with Fear, become **Mirror-Marked** until the scene ends. Mirror-Marked is a state defined only by the Crossing attempt below and has no hidden penalty.

**The Crossing attempt:** Once per round, the Breach may target one Mirror-Marked character. That character makes a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 15. On success, clear Mirror-Marked. On failure, the original is pulled behind the surface and a hostile Mirror Echo appears in their former zone. The player keeps control of the original and every decision.

**Mirror Echo:** Tier equals the original's Tier; Evasion `10 + Tier`; HP `4 × Tier`; Attack `+2 + Tier`; damage `Tier d6 Neural`; no Stress; immune to identity-changing effects. It may copy ordinary movement and attacks but cannot copy path resources, once-per-use features, artifacts, or a Death Move.

**Returning:** At the start of each trapped character's Spotlight, make a Presence Roll, DC 15. On success, return to the Echo's zone and remove the Echo. On Failure with Hope, communicate one sentence through the surface. On Failure with Fear, mark 1 Stress. An ally may spend an Action to cover or break the relevant surface, granting Advantage on the next return Roll. The character does not die from elapsed time and no Roll changes which character the player controls.

**Understanding the Breach:** A Knowledge Roll, DC 15, reveals all of the above procedure before the next Crossing attempt.
### THE PROBABILITY STORM (TIER 4)


*"I saw seven different things happen. Seven different outcomes. Then all of them collapsed into one. Not the one I wanted."*

**Description:** A zone where probability has broken. Instead of one outcome occurring, multiple outcomes exist simultaneously until observed, and observation itself becomes unreliable. Reality flickers between possibilities.

**Visual Signs:** Objects existing in multiple positions. Sounds from events that didn't happen. Contradictory evidence of different outcomes. A sense that every action branches.

**Effects:**

- **Probability Pressure:** at the start of each round, every character in the zone marks 1 Stress.
- **Branching Roll:** once per Spotlight, after a character makes a nonmatching Core Trait Roll and before narration, that player may reroll the Hope die and must use the new face. It may create a Critical Success; a matched result cannot be rerolled.
- **Unstable Position:** moving two bands during one Spotlight requires an Instinct Roll, DC 20. On failure move only one band; on Failure with Fear also become Dazed.
- **Pattern Reading:** Knowledge Roll, DC 15. On success one chosen ally has Advantage on their next Roll in the Storm; on a Critical Success choose two allies.
- **Forced Collapse:** Presence Roll, DC 20, once per scene. On success end Probability Pressure until the end of the next round. Failure with Fear marks 1 additional Stress on the user.

All outcomes resolve once and immediately. The Storm never makes two contradictory results simultaneously, never cancels matching dice, and never delegates a mechanical choice to a coin flip.

**Keeper Notes:** Describe unrealized alternatives as sensory echoes after the canonical outcome resolves. They are fiction, not additional results.


### THE VOID SCAR (TIER 5)


*"It's not a hole. It's an absence. The universe doesn't have a wound there, the universe never existed there. Never will. We need to leave. Now."*

**Description:** A region where reality has been permanently erased. Not damaged, not distorted, erased. The Void Scar is a place where nothing exists and nothing can exist. It grows slowly, consuming everything it touches.

**Visual Signs:** Absolute darkness that isn't dark, it's the absence of the concept of light. A boundary that the eye cannot focus on. The feeling of standing at the edge of existence.

**Effects:**

The boundary is always perceptible to ordinary sight or working sensors before a character reaches it. A navigation failure, Fear spend, random event, or forced movement cannot place a character across it without a final chance to react. If forced toward the boundary, make an Instinct Reaction Roll, DC 20, to stop at its edge. A character crosses only after the Keeper states the consequence and that character's player knowingly confirms the action.

- **Annihilation:** A character who knowingly enters the Scar takes 6d12 Void damage that prevents Armor Slot use. At 0 HP use Dying, Final, stabilization, and the voluntary Death Move normally. Unattended mundane objects and ordinary adversaries are erased. The boundary is always telegraphed and can never be crossed through a random event or Fear spend.

- **Expansion:** The Scar grows by 1 meter per year. Nothing has been found that slows this growth.

- **Memory Erosion:** This is descriptive only. It never removes a character's Experience, Feature, memory, Action, or knowledge without that player's consent.

- **Attraction:** This is descriptive only. It never compels movement, belief, or a player decision.

**No Navigation:**

Void Scars cannot be navigated. There is no safe passage through. The only valid strategy is avoidance.

**No Resolution:**

No known method can close a Void Scar. Precursor technology created them, possibly as weapons, possibly as mistakes, possibly as something else entirely. They are permanent.

**Keeper Notes:**

Void Scars exist to establish stakes. They're not meant to be "solved", they're meant to demonstrate that some

things are beyond the party's ability to fix. They're excellent for campaign-level threats that force difficult choices (the treasure is past the Scar; is it worth the risk?).


## 19.3: PRECURSOR RUIN GENERATION


When you need to create a Precursor site quickly, use the following tables.


### LOCATION TABLE (D12)


| D12 | PRIMARY LOCATION |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Asteroid (hollowed out) |
| **2** | Planet surface (desert/wasteland) |
| **3** | Planet surface (jungle/overgrown) |
| **4** | Underground (natural caverns modified) |
| **5** | Underwater (planet or moon) |
| **6** | Orbital station (damaged/decaying) |
| **7** | Dimensional pocket (accessed through portal) |
| **8** | Inside larger structure (ship, station, city) |
| **9** | Moon (surface or underground) |
| **10** | Gas giant atmosphere (floating structure) |
| **11** | Debris field (fragmented structure) |
| **12** | Impossible location (inside star, in void between galaxies, etc.) |


### ORIGINAL PURPOSE TABLE (D10)


| D10 | THE PRECURSORS BUILT THIS |
| --- | --- |


|  | FOR\... |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Research (scientific facility) |
| **2** | Residence (living space) |
| **3** | Manufacturing (production facility) |
| **4** | Defense (military installation) |
| **5** | Storage (vault or archive) |
| **6** | Transportation (hub or waypoint) |
| **7** | Religious/Cultural (temple or monument) |
| **8** | Medical (healing or modification facility) |
| **9** | Prison (containment facility) |
| **10** | Unknown (purpose cannot be determined) |


### CURRENT CONDITION TABLE (D8)


| D8 | CURRENT STATE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Pristine (appears recently abandoned) |
| **2** | Weathered (aged but structurally sound) |
| **3** | Damaged (partial structural failure) |
| **4** | Ruined (mostly collapsed, some areas accessible) |
| **5** | Overgrown (nature has reclaimed it) |
| **6** | Submerged (flooded or buried) |
| **7** | Active (systems still functioning) |
| **8** | Transformed (no longer resembles original purpose) |


### HAZARD DISTRIBUTION (D6)


| D6 | ANOMALY PRESENCE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Minimal (1-2 minor anomalies) |
| **2-3** | Moderate (3-4 anomalies of varying severity) |
| **4-5** | Heavy (5-6 anomalies, at least one Tier 3+) |
| **6** | Pervasive (anomalies everywhere; safe areas are rare) |


### TREASURE TABLE (D10)


| D10 | ARTIFACT POTENTIAL |
| --- | --- |
| **1-2** | Empty (already looted or never had anything) |
| **3-5** | Minor (1-2 Tier 1 artifacts, data fragments) |
| **6-7** | Moderate (1 Tier 2 artifact, valuable materials) |
| **8-9** | Significant (1 Tier 2 artifact, possible Tier 3) |
| **10** | Major (Tier 3 artifact guaranteed, possible Tier 4) |


### GUARDIANS TABLE (D8)


| D8 | WHAT STILL PROTECTS THIS |
| --- | --- |


|  | PLACE? |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Nothing (defenses long failed) |
| **2** | Automated systems (damaged but functional) |
| **3** | Creatures (native life that adapted to the ruins) |
| **4** | Squatters (other sapients have claimed the site) |
| **5** | Constructs (Precursor machines still on patrol) |
| **6** | Anomalies (the hazards ARE the guardians) |
| **7** | Cultists (worshippers protecting a holy site) |
| **8** | The Artifact (the treasure protects itself) |


### PUTTING IT TOGETHER: EXAMPLE


*Rolls: Location 7, Purpose 5, Condition 7, Hazards 5, Treasure 9, Guardians 5*

**Result:** A **dimensional pocket** (accessed through a portal) that was originally a **storage vault** and remains in **active** condition. There are **5-6 anomalies including at least one Tier 3+**. The vault contains a **significant treasure** (Tier 2 artifact, possible Tier 3) and is guarded by **Precursor constructs**.

**Interpretation:** This is an active archive, still maintaining its systems after millennia. The constructs patrol endlessly, protecting data and artifacts the Precursors stored. The anomalies are security measures, some deliberate, some the result of millennia of operation without maintenance. Getting in requires finding the portal; getting out requires surviving what's inside.


## 19.4: THE ECONOMY OF ARTIFACTS: SELLING TO POWERS


Selling a Precursor artifact is not like selling cargo. It's a major narrative event. You don't sell to shopkeepers; you sell to Powers, and Powers have agendas.


### THE BUYERS HOUSE AMARANTH (THE ARCHIVISTS)


*"We preserve. We study. We understand. Give us your discovery, and it will be cataloged, protected, and analyzed for the benefit of all."*

**Interested In:** Data, utility artifacts, historical items, the Codex of Silence

**Payment:** Wealth (Tier 5 Credits), access to secret lore, removal of Wanted status, political protection

**Risk Level:** Low. They will study it, not weaponize it\... probably.

**The Truth:** Amaranth genuinely preserves artifacts, but they also keep secrets. Items sold to them disappear into archives. You'll never know what they learned.


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 20-40 Cr | Access to archives |
| **2** | 60-100 Cr | Research partnership |
| **3** | 200-400 Cr | Political favor |
| **4** | Negotiated | Campaign-level reward |


### HOUSE KUROGANE (THE TECHNOCRATS)


*"Everything can be understood. Everything can be improved. Give us your discovery, and we will unlock its true potential."*

**Interested In:** Weapons, energy sources, cybernetics, the Genetic Archive

**Payment:** Experimental technology (Tier 4), prototype augmentations, technical support, research data

**Risk Level:** High. They will reverse-engineer it. They will weaponize it if possible.

**The Truth:** Kurogane's first question about any artifact is "How can we make more?" Their second is "How can we make it deadlier?"


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 15-30 Cr | Tech support |
| **2** | 50-80 Cr | Prototype equipment |
| **3** | 150-300 Cr | Experimental tech access |
| **4** | Negotiated | Campaign-level reward |


### HOUSE VALERIUS (THE AUCTIONEERS)


*"We don't buy artifacts. We broker them. Give us your discovery, and we'll find the buyer who values it most, for a reasonable percentage."*

**Interested In:** Anything valuable to anyone

**Payment:** Maximum market value minus 20-30% commission

**Risk Level:** Medium. They'll sell to whoever pays most, regardless of intent.


**The Truth:** Valerius will absolutely sell a weapon to someone who plans to use it. They're merchants, not moralists.


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 25-50 Cr | Market access |
| **2** | 80-150 Cr | Premium connections |
| **3** | 300-600 Cr | House protection |
| **4** | Negotiated | Auction (highest bidder) |


### HOUSE VOLKOV (THE WARRIORS)


*"Peace is a lie told by those too weak to fight. Give us your discovery, and we will test it against our enemies, for the glory of the strong."*

**Interested In:** Weapons, defensive systems, anything military, the Void Compass

**Payment:** Military support, trained personnel, vehicles, ships, combat technology

**Risk Level:** Very High. They will use it immediately against whoever they're fighting.

**The Truth:** Volkov won't study an artifact, they'll deploy it. If it causes a massacre, they'll call it a successful test.


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 15-25 Cr | Military supplies |
| **2** | 40-70 Cr | Personnel support |
| **3** | 100-250 Cr | Ship or vehicle |
| **4** | Negotiated | Fleet support |


### THE CHURCH OF THE ETERNAL VEIL


*"These are sacred relics, not mere objects. Give us your discovery, and it will be honored, protected, and used only as the Precursors intended."*

**Interested In:** Religious/cultural artifacts, Veil-affecting items, the Silence Bell

**Payment:** Spiritual services, sanctuary, political immunity, favor with the faithful

**Risk Level:** Variable. Some items they'll preserve; others they'll use for rituals with unpredictable results.

**The Truth:** The Church believes artifacts are messages from divine beings. They may use them in ways the Precursors never intended, based on theological interpretation.


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 10-20 Cr | Sanctuary |
| **2** | 30-60 Cr | Political immunity |
| **3** | 100-200 Cr | Church protection |
| **4** | Negotiated | Divine favor (whatever that means) |


### PRIVATE COLLECTORS


*"I must have it. Name your price."*

**Interested In:** Specific items based on collector obsession

**Payment:** Cash, no questions asked

**Risk Level:** Low for you. Unknown for everyone else.

**The Truth:** Private collectors vary wildly. Some are responsible preservationists. Some are dangerously unstable. Selling to unknowns means accepting that you don't know what happens next.


| ARTIFACT TIER | PAYMENT RANGE | ADDITIONAL |
| --- | --- | --- |


|  |  | BENEFITS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1** | 30-60 Cr | Discretion |
| **2** | 100-200 Cr | No records |
| **3** | 400-800 Cr | Ongoing relationship |
| **4** | Auction only | Unpredictable |


### THE CONSEQUENCES OF SELLING


What happens after you sell an artifact?

**Immediate:**

- Payment received

- Reputation change with buyer (improved) and their rivals (worsened)

- Heat reduction (selling to Houses is "legitimate")

**Long-term:**

- The artifact is used according to the buyer's agenda

- If weaponized: people may die because of your sale

- If researched: the buyer gains knowledge advantage

- If preserved: the artifact is "safe" but inaccessible

- If auctioned: you don't control the final destination

**Story Hooks from Sales:**

- The artifact you sold is killing people. Do you feel responsible?

- The artifact you sold revealed something dangerous. The buyer wants to silence you.

- The artifact you sold is now being used against people you care about.

- The buyer wants more. They're willing to fund expeditions, but they own what you find.

# CHAPTER 20: NARRATIVE TOOLS & TABLES

*"Every Keeper needs a bag of tricks, generators that create problems faster than players can solve them, tables that inject chaos when sessions grow predictable, and NPCs ready to step on stage when you need a face for the villain you just invented. This is that bag."*

*Keeper's Note, Session 47*


## INTRODUCTION: THE ART OF IMPROVISATION


No session survives contact with players intact. The elaborate plot you prepared? They'll ignore it to follow a random NPC you mentioned once. The carefully designed heist? They'll solve it in five minutes or complicate it for three sessions. The faction politics you mapped? Irrelevant once they steal the ambassador's shuttle.

This chapter provides the tools to improvise with confidence. When players zig, these tables let you zag. When you need a homeworld in thirty seconds, a tension to complicate the scene, or an NPC with depth and motivation, these generators deliver.

Use these tools liberally. Randomness creates surprises, not just for players, but for Keepers. The best sessions often emerge from combinations you never would have planned.


## 20.1: SPECIES TENSION GENERATOR


The galaxy is populated by species with deep histories, ancient grudges, and cultural friction. Use these tables when you need instant inter-species tension or want to add complexity to encounters involving multiple ancestries.


### HISTORICAL TENSION TABLE (D12)


Roll when two species interact and you need history between them:


| D12 | TENSION SOURCE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Ancient War: Their ancestors fought a devastating conflict. Neither side has forgotten. |
| **2** | Resource Competition: They once competed for the same vital resource. One species won; one nearly went extinct. |
| **3** | Religious Conflict: Their belief systems are fundamentally incompatible. Each considers the other heretical. |
| **4** | Betrayal: One species betrayed the other during a crisis. Trust was shattered permanently. |
| **5** | Subjugation: One species enslaved or colonized the other. The scars remain. |
| **6** | Territorial Dispute: They both claim the same region of space. The dispute is "resolved" but never forgotten. |
| **7** | Cultural Disgust: Their customs are mutually repulsive. Each finds the other's practices barbaric. |
| **8** | Economic Rivalry: They compete for the same markets. Every transaction is a battlefield. |
| **9** | Biological Incompatibility: Something about their biology (pheromones, appearance, sounds) triggers instinctive discomfort. |
| **10** | Stolen Technology: One species claims the other stole their innovations. The accused deny it. |
| **11** | Prophecy: One species' religion includes prophecy about the other, as enemies, as servants, or worse. |
| **12** | The Great Silence: One species blames the other for events during the Silence. Evidence is fragmentary but damning. |


### CURRENT FRICTION TABLE (D8)


Roll to determine how tension manifests today:


| D8 | CURRENT EXPRESSION |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Cold Politeness: They interact formally, correctly, and with barely concealed contempt. |
| **2** | Segregation: They avoid each other. Mixed-species spaces are uncomfortable for both. |
| **3** | Legal Discrimination: One species faces institutional barriers in areas controlled by the other. |
| **4** | Economic Warfare: Trade restrictions, tariffs, and commercial sabotage are constant. |
| **5** | Proxy Conflicts: They fight through intermediaries, supporting opposite sides in other conflicts. |
| **6** | Occasional Violence: Hate crimes occur. Both sides have extremists. Officials look away. |
| **7** | Diplomatic Posturing: Every interaction becomes a negotiation; every negotiation becomes a contest. |
| **8** | Active Reconciliation: Both sides are trying to heal, but old wounds keep reopening. |


### PERSONAL REACTION TABLE (D6)


When an individual from one species meets an individual from the other:


| D6 | PERSONAL STANCE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Hardcore Bigot: Embraces all prejudices. Will not cooperate. May become hostile. |
| **2** | Casual Prejudice: Makes assumptions. Uses slurs "without meaning anything by it." |
| **3** | Uncomfortable: Wants to be progressive but finds interaction difficult. |
| **4** | Professionally Neutral: Judges individuals by actions, not species. Still aware of history. |
| **5** | Actively Welcoming: Goes out of their way to reject prejudice. Sometimes awkwardly. |
| **6** | Personal Exception: "I don't like [species], but you're different." |


### USING SPECIES TENSION


**In Negotiations:** If the optional Tension module from Alien Species is active, use its exact Wary/Tense/Hostile/Violent effects. Otherwise established prejudice may impose Disadvantage or move a social DC one rung, never both.

**In Combat:** Enemies may target members of hated species first, or refuse to take them prisoner.

**In Social Situations:** NPCs may refuse service, provide false information, or actively obstruct characters of certain species.

**As Complication:** A simple transaction becomes complicated when the merchant realizes who they're dealing with.

### PUTTING IT TOGETHER: EXAMPLE


*Rolls: World Type 3, Challenge 1, Power 7, Culture 6, Crisis 8*

**Result:** A **Mining World** with **Extreme Temperature** problems, controlled by a **Criminal Syndicate**, with a culture of **Survival Pragmatism**, currently experiencing **Mysterious Disappearances**.

**Interpretation:** A frozen rock where miners extract rare minerals under brutal conditions. The official government collapsed years ago; now criminal bosses run the company towns. People do whatever they must to

survive another shift. Recently, miners have been vanishing from the deep shafts, no bodies, no explanation. The bosses don't care, but the workers are getting scared.


## 20.3: NPC QUICK-BUILD TABLES


When you need an NPC instantly, these tables provide personality, motivation, and conflict in seconds.


### ROLE TABLE (D20)

| D12 | PERSONALITY |
| --- | --- |

### QUICK STATS

When you need mechanical statistics quickly, choose values inside the listed range and add only the Features required by the concept.

| TIER AND ROLE | EVASION | ATTACK | DAMAGE | HP | STRESS | THRESHOLDS | EXTRA |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 Minion | 10-13 | +1 to +3 | 1d4 or 1d6 | 1 | - | None | 0 Armor Slots unless a Feature says otherwise. |
| Tier 2 Standard | 12-15 | +3 to +5 | 1d8+1 or 2d6 | 8-14 | 3-6 | Major 7-12 / Severe 14-22 | 0 Armor Slots unless a Feature says otherwise. |
| Tier 3 Elite | 14-18 | +5 to +8 | 2d8+2 or 3d6 | 15-30 | 6-10 | Major 9-15 / Severe 18-30 | 1 Fear Ability. |
| Tier 4 Boss | 13-19 | +6 to +9 | 3d8+4 or 4d6+5 | 35-80 | 8-15 | Major 12-30 / Severe 24-60 | 2-3 Fear Abilities. |

NPC Traits are descriptive selectors for Rolls, not a substitute for Evasion, Attack, Stress, Thresholds, or Armor Slots.


## 20.4: PARAGON NPC GALLERY


These fully detailed NPCs can be dropped into any campaign as allies, enemies, or complications.


### COMMANDER ELENA VOSS


**Role:** Former House Volkov Military Officer

**Species:** Human \| **Age:** 47

**Appearance:** Steel-gray hair cut military-short. Prosthetic left arm (military grade, concealed weapons). Burn scars across neck and jaw. Eyes that have seen too much.

**Personality:** Disciplined, pragmatic, haunted. Speaks in clipped sentences. Never wastes words. Drinks alone but not to excess, just enough to sleep.

**Background:** Voss commanded a battalion during the Frontier Suppression. She followed orders that resulted in civilian casualties, orders she now believes were unnecessary. She resigned her commission rather than face internal promotion for the "success." Now she works private security, taking jobs that let her protect people rather than harm them.


**Motivation:** Redemption through action. She can't undo what she did, but she can balance the scales.

**Secret:** She has evidence that the Suppression orders came from someone currently positioned for High Command. If revealed, it could trigger a Volkov civil war.

**Hooks:**

- Hire her as security for a dangerous transport

- She's protecting someone the players need to reach

- She needs help accessing a Volkov archive to retrieve her evidence

**Stats (Tier 3 Leader):**

- Evasion: 14 | HP: 28 | Stress: 8
- Thresholds: Major 15 / Severe 30 | Armor Slots: 5

- Strength +3, Agility +2, Finesse +1, Knowledge +2, Instinct +3, Presence +2

- Attack: +5, Damage 2d6+3

- **Special:** Tactical Assessment (once per scene, all allies gain +2 to next attack)

- **Equipment:** Military combat armor, integrated arm weapons (pistol + blade), encrypted communicator


### "SUNSHINE" MALIK TORRES


**Role:** Black Market Fixer

**Species:** Human \| **Age:** 34

**Appearance:** Perpetual smile that never reaches his eyes. Expensive clothes, slightly too flashy. Gold tooth. Always has a drink in hand but never seems intoxicated.

**Personality:** Charming, manipulative, amoral. Treats everything like a game he's winning. Genuinely likes people, which makes using them easier.

**Background:** Born in the Neon-City Undercity, raised by a mother who worked three jobs to keep him fed. He swore he'd never be poor again. Now he facilitates deals between people who can't be seen together, takes his percentage, and asks no questions.

**Motivation:** Wealth and the freedom it brings. Also, the game itself, he loves being the one who makes things happen.

**Secret:** He's been paying for his mother's medical treatment at a Core World hospital. House Valerius discovered this and uses it as leverage, he occasionally feeds them information about clients.

**Hooks:**

- The players need something only Sunshine can acquire

- Sunshine needs the players to handle a deal that's gone wrong

- Someone is killing Sunshine's contacts, and he needs protection

**Stats (Tier 2 Leader):**

- Evasion: 13 | HP: 14 | Stress: 6
- Thresholds: Major 10 / Severe 18 | Armor Slots: 2

- Strength +0, Agility +2, Finesse +3, Knowledge +2, Instinct +2, Presence +4

- Attack: +3, Damage 1d6 Physical (holdout pistol)

- **Special:** "I Know a Guy" (can provide introduction to any Black Market contact, DC 10)

- **Equipment:** Concealed pistol, credit chips (clean), emergency transponder, three fake IDs


### DR. YUKI TANAKA


**Role:** Ripperdoc / Underground Surgeon

**Species:** Human \| **Age:** 52

**Appearance:** Weathered hands with visible augmentation interfaces. Gray-streaked hair pulled back. Eyes magnified by permanent surgical lenses. Lab coat that's never quite clean.

**Personality:** Detached, professional, quietly compassionate. Treats bodies as machines to be fixed. Never asks how patients got hurt. Has a weakness for hopeless cases.

**Background:** Trained at House Kurogane's premier medical academy. Left after refusing to participate in non-consensual augmentation experiments on prisoners. Now operates a clinic in the Rust Belt, treating anyone who needs help, no questions, no records.

**Motivation:** Save lives without participating in systems that destroy them.

**Secret:** She still has access codes to Kurogane medical databases. She uses them occasionally to steal research that could help her patients. Kurogane knows someone is accessing the system but hasn't traced it to her, yet.

**Hooks:**

- Players need illegal augmentations installed

- Dr. Tanaka needs specific medical supplies from a Kurogane facility

- A patient in her care has information enemies want

**Stats (Tier 2 Standard):**

- Evasion: 13 | HP: 10 | Stress: 5
- Thresholds: Major 8 / Severe 15 | Armor Slots: 0

- Strength +0, Agility +2, Finesse +4, Knowledge +4, Instinct +2, Presence +1

- Attack: +1, Damage 1d4 Physical (surgical tools, improvised)

- **Special:** Master Surgeon (all medical procedures gain +4; can install augmentations without normal facilities)

- **Equipment:** Surgical toolkit, medical supplies, illegal anesthetics, patient records (encrypted)


### CARDINAL THRACE


**Role:** Church of the Eternal Veil Inquisitor

**Species:** Human \| **Age:** 61


**Appearance:** Tall, gaunt, radiating certainty. White robes of the Church. Eyes that seem to look through people. Voice like honey over iron.

**Personality:** Utterly convinced of their righteousness. Patient, methodical, terrifying. Believes in redemption, even if it must be forced.

**Background:** Rose through Church ranks through genuine devotion and genuine ruthlessness. Now investigates threats to the faith, heretics, Precursor corruption, Veil-touched individuals who haven't submitted to Church oversight.

**Motivation:** Protect the faithful from spiritual contamination. Bring the corrupt back to the light, or remove them from it permanently.

**Secret:** Thrace experienced a genuine Veil vision years ago that shook their faith. They've never spoken of it. They're not sure if they're still a believer or just going through motions. The doubt terrifies them.

**Hooks:**

- Thrace is investigating something near the players

- A friend of the players has been taken by Thrace for "questioning"

- Thrace believes a player character is spiritually contaminated

**Stats (Tier 3 Leader):**

- Evasion: 16 | HP: 24 | Stress: 10
- Thresholds: Major 12 / Severe 24 | Armor Slots: 3 (blessed robes)

- Strength +1, Agility +1, Finesse +1, Knowledge +3, Instinct +4, Presence +4

- Attack: +6, Damage 2d6 Neural (faith-weapon)

- **Special:** Voice of Authority (once per scene, command must be obeyed unless target succeeds on a DC 15 Instinct Reaction Roll)

- **Special:** See the Corruption (automatically detects Veil-touched abilities and Precursor artifacts within 10m)

- **Equipment:** Faith-weapon (ceremonial blade), Church credentials, inquisitorial authority


### KRYX-SEVEN-BREAKING-DAWN


**Role:** Kryx Pack-Leader / Salvage Boss

**Species:** Kryx \| **Age:** Unknown (mature adult)

**Appearance:** Larger than average Kryx, scarred from countless fights. Missing two fingers on left hand.

Decorated with salvaged tech woven into fur. Moves with predator confidence.

**Personality:** Direct, honorable (by Kryx standards), surprisingly fair. Values strength but respects cunning. Protects pack absolutely.

**Background:** Led their pack from refugee status to controlling significant Rust Belt salvage territory. Built reputation through fair dealing and brutal enforcement. Other packs respect or fear them.

**Motivation:** Pack prosperity and security. Everything else is secondary.

**Secret:** They've discovered a pre-Silence military vessel in the deep debris, intact, dormant, valuable beyond measure. They're trying to figure out how to claim it without starting a war.

**Hooks:**

- Players need salvage from Kryx-controlled territory

- Kryx-Seven needs outsiders for a job they can't use pack members for

- A rival is trying to unite other packs against Kryx-Seven

**Stats (Tier 3 Bruiser):**

- Evasion: 14 | HP: 32 | Stress: 6
- Thresholds: Major 15 / Severe 30 | Armor Slots: 4 (salvage armor)

- Strength +4, Agility +3, Finesse +1, Knowledge +1, Instinct +3, Presence +3

- Attack: +5, Damage 2d8+4 Physical (power-claw)

- **Special:** Pack Tactics (allies adjacent to Kryx-Seven gain +2 to attack)

- **Special:** Territorial Claim (knows exact location of everything valuable in their territory)

- **Equipment:** Custom power-claw, salvage armor, pack communication system

| **3** | A human settlement is demanding independence from House control. They're asking for help, but success means making enemies of a Great House. |
| **4** | Ancient human religious texts have been discovered that contradict Church of the Eternal Veil doctrine. The Church wants them destroyed; scholars want them |
|  | preserved. |

|  | using alien biology. |

|  | asserting authority over human systems. Their claim might be legitimate. |
| **7** | Human refugees from a destroyed colony are being denied settlement rights. |
|  | They're getting desperate, and desperate people do desperate things. |
| **8** | A human supremacist group is planning an attack on a multi-species station. They |
|  | have inside help from someone in station security. |

| **8** | A Kryllian hermit claims to have a pre-Silence Kryllian artifact that proves their species had contact with the Precursors. Others want to see it. Others want it destroyed. |

## 20.6: CREW FRICTION GENERATOR


Crew friction is the engine of long-running campaigns. When the crew agrees on everything, the table runs out

of conflict to play with. When the crew has live tensions, every decision is dramatic. The tables below generate friction *between* crew members, the kind that doesn't need an external enemy to surface.

Use these tables between sessions to seed character moments, or roll mid-session when a Keeper Fear spend wants narrative weight beyond a mechanical setback.


### FRICTION SOURCE (D10)


| D10 | SOURCE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Disagreement over a recent crew decision; the consequences are now visible and one member was right. |
| **2** | An old debt one crew member owes another has become inconvenient to repay. |
| **3** | One crew member's secret has nearly surfaced, and another knows. |
| **4** | A romantic or close-friend connection one crew member is hiding from the others has become impossible to hide further. |
| **5** | One crew member's ancestry-specific need (Bloomstrider nutrition, Synthetic maintenance, Kryx pack contact) has been deprioritized one too many times. |
| **6** | A non-crew NPC has explicitly preferred one crew member over the others, and the others noticed. |
| **7** | A score the crew completed produced an unequal payout, and the inequality has not been addressed. |
| **8** | One crew member's character flaw (gambling, stress eating, lashing out) is impacting crew operations. |
| **9** | A philosophical disagreement about a mission's morality has been deferred but never resolved. |
| **10** | One crew member is grieving a loss the others have moved past. |


### FRICTION SURFACE (D8)


How the friction breaks into the open:


| D8 | SURFACE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | A sharp comment over breakfast in the galley. |
| **2** | An equipment shortage one crew member secretly caused by hoarding. |
| **3** | A mission-critical decision where the friction influences strategy. |
| **4** | A drunk confession at a port, partially overheard. |
| **5** | A request for privacy that everyone reads as exclusion. |
| **6** | An unsent message draft found on a shared terminal. |
| **7** | A silent retreat to one's cabin that lasts longer than it should. |
| **8** | A confrontation in front of an NPC, exposing the crew's tension to an outsider. |


### FRICTION RESOLUTION STAKE (D6)


What the resolution requires:


| D6 | RESOLUTION STAKE |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | A direct conversation, properly held, no jokes deflecting. |
| **2** | A shared task that requires both parties to cooperate without supervision. |
| **3** | A gesture of acknowledgment, possibly material, possibly only spoken. |
| **4** | A confession of something the resentful party has been hiding too. |
| **5** | A formal apology with witnesses (rare; usually only in crews with strict cultural protocols, e.g. Kryx packs). |
| **6** | An external event large enough to make the friction trivial by comparison. |


## 20.7: DOWNTIME OUTCOME TABLES


Crews need downtime to recover, but downtime is its own scene. The tables below generate texture and surprise for the periods between missions, when the crew is officially resting but the campaign continues.


### GENERAL DOWNTIME RESULT (D12)


Roll once per crew member per downtime period:


| D12 | RESULT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | An old contact reappears with bad news. |
| **2** | A previously-completed mission generates an unexpected aftershock (someone the crew thought they'd left behind, an item they thought they'd disposed of). |
| **3** | An item the crew member owns malfunctions or develops a quirk. |
| **4** | A romantic interest, real or pursued, makes a move (positive or negative). |
| **5** | A piece of personal correspondence arrives (family, mentor, past employer). |
| **6** | A small windfall: 1d4 Credits found, given, or won. |
| **7** | A small loss: 1d4 Credits stolen, spent, or owed. |
| **8** | The crew member learns something useful through eavesdropping or chance encounter. |
| **9** | An old debt is called in. |
| **10** | Name one Experience the crew member has not used recently. It cannot be invoked on the first otherwise eligible Roll of the next mission, then returns normally. |
| **11** | The crew member sleeps badly all week, gain 1 Stress at start of next mission. |
| **12** | A surprising piece of good news the crew member had given up hoping for. |


### CONNECTION CULTIVATION (D8)


When a crew member spends downtime specifically pursuing a Connection (per Chapter 8 of the Corebook):


| D8 | RESULT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The Connection is unavailable; the crew member learns why and the why is |
|  | concerning. |
| **2** | The Connection has a problem they need help with before they can be of use. |
| **3** | Brief, formal exchange. The Connection remains at current standing; +1 to next |
|  | interaction. |
| **4** | A useful piece of information is shared. The Keeper provides 1 actionable fact. |
| **5** | The Connection introduces the crew member to one of their own Connections, |
|  | expanding the network. |
| **6** | A favor is owed in either direction, depending on what the crew member needed. |
| **7** | A genuine moment of human connection, the kind that makes the relationship matter. Connection standing increases. |
| **8** | An unexpected gift, a piece of useful equipment, a name, an opportunity worth 1d4 Credits or a future Favor. |


### STRESS RECOVERY ACTIVITY (D10)


When a crew member spends downtime on stress recovery, roll to determine the activity's character:


| D10 | ACTIVITY |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Solitary meditation, contemplation, or prayer. -2 Stress. |
| **2** | A physical regimen that doubles as conditioning. -1 Stress, +1 to first Strength roll next mission. |
| **3** | Time with a romantic interest. -2 Stress, generates a Connection check the next time the relationship matters. |
| **4** | Drinking, gambling, or other vices. Clear 2 Stress, then roll d6: on 1-3 record one declared social or financial complication that appears during the next mission; on 4-6 there is no complication. |
| **5** | Crafting, repair work, hobby maintenance. -1 Stress, restore a Damaged piece of personal equipment. |
| **6** | Time spent with one specific crew member, deepening that relationship. -1 Stress for both. |
| **7** | An unscheduled adventure that becomes a memory, the kind of side-quest the table will reference years later. -3 Stress, but no mechanical benefit. |
| **8** | A confrontation with a personal flaw, examined deliberately. -1 Stress, gain 1 path resource (Hope, or 1 Effort if Sleeping) at start of next mission. |
| **9** | Productive rest. Full Stress recovery and one extra Hope. |
| **10** | Disrupted rest. -1 Stress, but the crew member was working on something useful; gain 1 Resource or 1d4 Credits worth of progress on a personal project. |


## 20.8: MISSION COMPLICATION GENERATOR


Use these tables when a mission needs a mid-act surprise that wasn't planned. Roll any time a moment feels too clean.


### COMPLICATION TRIGGER (D6)


| D6 | WHEN THE COMPLICATION |
| --- | --- |


|  | ENTERS |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | At mission start, during briefing or preparation. |
| **2** | At approach, while the crew is moving toward the objective. |
| **3** | At first contact, the moment of initial engagement. |
| **4** | At midpoint, when the crew thinks they've stabilized. |
| **5** | At climax, during the critical action. |
| **6** | At extraction, during the supposed "win." |


### COMPLICATION TYPE (D20)


| D20 | COMPLICATION |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | A second team is on the same job. |
| **2** | The objective is not where intelligence said it would be. |
| **3** | The objective is not what intelligence said it was. |
| **4** | A bystander witnesses what should have been clean. |
| **5** | A crew member's old enemy is present in an unrelated capacity. |
| **6** | An ally turns out to be working against the crew. |
| **7** | An apparent enemy turns out to be working with the crew. |
| **8** | The client's information was deliberately misleading. |
| **9** | A faction the crew thought was uninvolved declares interest. |
| **10** | A weather, environmental, or substrate event disrupts plans. |
| **11** | Equipment failure at a critical moment. |
| **12** | A crew member's personal connection is on-site and complicates loyalties. |
| **13** | The authorities arrive earlier than expected. |
| **14** | The authorities are already there in disguise. |
| **15** | The objective has its own agenda and contacts the crew. |
| **16** | A second client appears, offering double for the crew to switch sides. |
| **17** | A rival broker exposes the crew's involvement to deflect Heat from themselves. |
| **18** | A previous mission's loose end resurfaces. |
| **19** | The Veil Rip locally intensifies; substrate phenomena interfere with technology. |
| **20** | The mission is a test by a faction the crew did not know was watching. |


### COMPLICATION SEVERITY (D6)


| D6 | SEVERITY |
| --- | --- |
| **1-2** | Minor: complicates this scene only, no lasting impact. |
| **3-4** | Significant: changes the mission's terms, but the original objective remains achievable. |
| **5** | Major: forces the crew to choose between original objective and new threat. |
| **6** | Critical: the mission becomes survival; original objective is lost or transformed entirely. |

# CHAPTER 21: THE "ONE LAST JOB" MISSION GENERATOR

*"Every scavenger has a 'last job', the score that'll let them retire, the payout that'll clear their debts, the run that'll finally make everything right. Funny thing about last jobs: there's always another one after."*

*Sly Marlo, The Fixer*


## INTRODUCTION: THE ANATOMY OF A SCORE


Black Market missions follow a familiar pattern. A client has a problem. The problem requires skills that legitimate channels can't provide. The reward is substantial, but so are the risks. Something always goes wrong.

This chapter provides a complete framework for generating Black Market missions on the fly. Roll on the tables, connect the results, and you have an evening's adventure, or the foundation of a multi-session campaign arc.

The "One Last Job" Generator creates missions with:

- **A Client**, Who's hiring and why

- **A Job**, What needs to be done

- **A Twist**, What complication emerges

- **Stakes**, What happens if the crew fails

Every job should feel like it could be "the one", the score that changes everything. Whether it actually is depends on how the dice fall.

## 21.4: SAMPLE MISSIONS (FULLY WRITTEN)


### MISSION 1: THE GILDED CAGE


**Client:** Wealthy merchant (Resource Level 4, Reliability 4)

**The Job:** Extraction. The client's daughter has been "recruited" into the Church of the Eternal Veil's inner circle. She went willingly, but the client believes she was manipulated. They want her out, alive, unharmed, and before her "final initiation" in three days.

**Location:** Church monastery on a remote moon. Security Level 4 (Professional, the Church takes its initiates seriously).

**Reward:** 75 Credits plus House contacts.

**The Twist:** The daughter doesn't want to leave. She genuinely believes. Also, her "final initiation" involves a Precursor artifact that grants visions, she's already partially bonded to it. Removing her might damage her mind.

**Complications:**

- Church security includes Veil-touched sensitives who can detect hostile intent

- The daughter has friends among the initiates who will protect her

- Cardinal Thrace (from Chapter 20) is overseeing the initiation

- A rival faction is also trying to acquire the artifact

**Resolution Options:**

- Convince the daughter to leave willingly (extremely difficult Social challenge)

- Steal her against her will (she'll fight back; possible permanent psychological damage)

- Destroy the artifact (ends the bonding but may harm all initiates)

- Negotiate with the Church (they might trade her for something valuable)

- Expose whatever manipulation was used (if any exists)

**Heat Generated:** +2 minimum (Church involvement); +4 if violence occurs


### MISSION 2: THE DEAD MAN'S CARGO


**Client:** Unknown patron (Resource Level 5, Reliability 3)

**The Job:** Smuggling. Pick up a sealed cargo container from a dead drop in the Rust Belt. Deliver it to coordinates in deep space. Do not open the container. Do not scan the container. Do not ask questions.

**Location:** Pickup: Rust Belt salvage yard. Delivery: Empty space at edge of system.

**Reward:** 100 Credits. Half on pickup, half on delivery.

**The Twist:** The container holds a person, a political prisoner being transported to execution. They're alive, barely. They know something someone wants silenced.

**Secondary Twist:** The delivery coordinates are an ambush. The patron doesn't want the prisoner delivered; they want the crew to take the fall for "kidnapping" while the prisoner disappears permanently.

**Complications:**

- The prisoner will die without medical attention within 24 hours

- Opening the container voids the contract (and triggers a tracking beacon)

- House Volkov is looking for the prisoner, they want them alive for interrogation

- The patron has backup crews ready to intercept if the primary crew balks

**Resolution Options:**

- Deliver as contracted (prisoner dies; crew gets paid but carries guilt)

- Save the prisoner, break contract (make enemy of powerful patron)

- Sell prisoner to Volkov (payment plus Heat from new enemy)

- Expose the patron (requires investigation; potential massive payoff if patron is important enough)

- Stage the prisoner's death and help them disappear (complex but rewarding)

**Heat Generated:** +1 for smuggling; +3 if prisoner situation becomes public


### MISSION 3: THE MEMORY THIEF


**Client:** Corrupt official (Resource Level 4, Reliability 2)

**The Job:** Information theft. A House Kurogane researcher has developed memory extraction technology, the ability to copy memories from a living brain. The client wants the research data stolen before Kurogane can weaponize it.

**Location:** Kurogane orbital research station. Security Level 5 (Elite).

**Reward:** 90 Credits plus the client will "lose" any outstanding warrants against crew members.

**The Twist:** The client doesn't want to prevent weaponization, they want to sell the technology to the highest bidder. Also, the researcher knows the crew is coming; they want to defect and will help in exchange for extraction.

**Secondary Twist:** The memory extraction technology works. The researcher has already used it, on themselves. They have copies of important memories from Kurogane executives in their head. They're worth far more than the data.

**Complications:**

- Kurogane station has Synthetic security that can't be bribed or deceived


- The researcher has a family on-station who can't be abandoned

- Multiple factions are converging on the station for the same research

- The extraction subject makes a Strength Reaction Roll, DC 20. On failure take 4d10 Neural damage; at 0 HP enter Dying normally. On success copy the stated memory and mark 2 Stress. Matching dice remain Critical Success, and the procedure never kills by percentage.

**Resolution Options:**

- Steal data, leave researcher (client is happy; researcher probably dies)

- Extract researcher, negotiate new deal (client may betray; researcher is valuable)

- Destroy the research (no one gets it; multiple enemies created)

- Acquire research and sell it yourself (maximum profit, maximum Heat)

- Expose the client's intentions to appropriate authorities (trade client for reduced Heat)

**Heat Generated:** +3 minimum (Kurogane involvement); +5 if anyone dies


### MISSION 4: ONE NIGHT IN NEON-CITY


**Client:** Criminal syndicate (Resource Level 3, Reliability 4)

**The Job:** Protection. The Syndicate is hosting a meeting with a rival organization to negotiate territory. They need neutral security, people who aren't affiliated with either side. One night. Keep everyone alive.

**Location:** Private venue in Neon-City Undercity. Security Level 3 (Enhanced, but the crew IS the security).

**Reward:** 40 Credits plus Syndicate reputation and future job opportunities.

**The Twist:** One of the attendees is planning an assassination, but the crew doesn't know which one or who the target is. Signs will emerge throughout the evening.

**Secondary Twist:** The assassination target is the crew's client. The rival organization set up this meeting specifically to kill them in a way that couldn't be traced back.

**Complications:**

- Both sides have brought hidden weapons despite agreements

- The venue has secret exits that could be used for escape or ambush

- House Valerius has the place under surveillance for unrelated reasons

- A third party (maybe Mama K) has sold information to both sides about the crew

**Resolution Options:**

- Identify assassin before they strike (investigation during social event)

- Prevent assassination openly (breaks neutrality; ally with target's faction)

- Let assassination happen (contract technically fulfilled; reputation damaged)

- Turn tables and expose the rival organization's plot (creates war; crew picks side)

- Extract client before assassination can occur (contract fulfilled differently)

**Heat Generated:** +2 if violence occurs; +4 if someone important dies


### MISSION 5: THE LAST VOYAGE OF THE STELLAR DREAM


**Client:** Desperate individual (Resource Level 6, they'll give everything, Reliability 6)

**The Job:** Rescue. The client's partner was aboard a luxury liner, the *Stellar Dream*, when it suffered catastrophic drive failure. The ship is adrift in the Veil's edge, official rescue was called off after three days. The client believes survivors remain.

**Location:** Deep space, Veil-adjacent. The *Stellar Dream* itself. Security Level: N/A (the ship is the threat).

**Reward:** Everything the client has, their business, their savings, their future. Approximately 60 Credits of tangible value.

**The Twist:** There are survivors, sort of. The *Stellar Dream* drifted through a Veil anomaly. Time moved differently inside. For the survivors, it's been weeks. They've changed. Some have been Veil-touched. Some have gone mad. Some have become something else entirely.

**Secondary Twist:** The client's partner is alive, but they don't want to leave. The Veil showed them something. They believe they have a purpose now. They won't come willingly.

**Complications:**

- The *Stellar Dream* is unstable, Veil anomalies make navigation hazardous

- Survivor factions have formed; some are hostile to rescuers

- Something else is on the ship now, something that came through with them

- Official rescue was called off because someone important was aboard and their death needs to stay hidden

**Resolution Options:**

- Full rescue (extract everyone willing; leave those who refuse)

- Targeted rescue (find the partner specifically; ignore other survivors)

- Mercy mission (the survivors are too far gone; ending their existence might be kindest)


- Investigation (find out what really happened; the information might be worth more than any rescue)

- Retreat (the ship is too dangerous; take what you can and run)

**Heat Generated:** +0 (it's technically a rescue mission); +3 if you bring back Veil-touched survivors without reporting them


## 21.5: CREATING CUSTOM BLACK MARKET ADVENTURES


### THE FORMULA


Every great Black Market mission follows a simple structure:

1. **The Hook:** Why should the crew take this job?

2. **The Challenge:** What makes the job difficult?

3. **The Twist:** What unexpected complication arises?

4. **The Choice:** What moral/practical decision must be made?

5. **The Consequence:** What happens based on that choice?


### BUILDING THE HOOK


The hook must answer: "Why would the crew risk this?"

**Strong Hooks:**

- The reward is exceptional (money, influence, items)

- The job connects to personal goals (revenge, redemption, obligation)

- Refusal has consequences (threats, lost opportunities, damaged reputation)

- The mystery is compelling (what are they really stealing? why does the client need this?)

**Weak Hooks:**

- "There's a job" (no stakes, no investment)

- Generic reward without context

- No personal connection to crew or campaign


### BUILDING THE CHALLENGE


The challenge should require:

- **Multiple skill sets**, Jobs that only need one character are boring

- **Decision points**, Choices between approaches (loud vs. quiet, fast vs. safe)

- **Environmental factors**, Location should affect tactics

- **Opposition with personality**, Enemies should be memorable, not generic


### BUILDING THE TWIST


Good twists:

- **Were foreshadowed**, Players should be able to look back and see the signs

- **Change the equation**, New information requires new decisions

- **Create moral complexity**, Simple jobs become complicated

- **Connect to larger narratives**, Twists that tie into campaign themes are most satisfying

Bad twists:

- "Gotcha" moments that punish player success

- Random complications with no connection to established elements

- Twists that remove player agency entirely

- Reveals that make previous decisions meaningless


### BUILDING THE CHOICE


The best Black Market missions force choices between:

- **Money vs. Morality**, The profitable option hurts someone

- **Loyalty vs. Self-Interest**, Standing by allies costs something

- **Short-term vs. Long-term**, Quick wins create future problems

- **Known vs. Unknown**, Safe choices vs. mysterious opportunities


### BUILDING THE CONSEQUENCES


Consequences should:

- **Follow logically** from choices made

- **Affect future sessions**, The galaxy should remember

- **Scale appropriately**, Small choices, small consequences; big choices, big consequences

- **Create new opportunities**, Consequences become hooks for future missions


### QUICK MISSION GENERATION CHECKLIST


□ Roll or choose Client (type, motivation, resources, reliability)

□ Roll or choose Job (type, location, security, time pressure)

□ Roll or choose Twist (what, severity, timing)

□ Determine reward based on difficulty and client resources

□ Calculate Heat based on job type and potential complications

□ Connect to campaign themes or player backstories if possible


□ Prepare 2-3 possible resolution paths

□ Note NPCs who might appear (use Chapter 20 quick-build if needed)

□ Identify Action Rolls likely to be required

□ Write one sentence summary: "The crew must [JOB] for [CLIENT] despite [TWIST]"


## 21.6: SPECIALTY MISSION TYPES


The Client + Job + Twist generator produces a generic mission. The tables below add texture specific to *what kind* of operation the crew is running. Roll on the appropriate sub-table when the mission's character is clear.


### HEIST SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS HEIST DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | Time-locked: the vault opens once per day for ninety seconds. |
| **2** | Counter-team: a rival crew is hitting the same target on the same night. |
| **3** | Living vault: the security system is biological and reads emotions. |
| **4** | Asset is alive: the target is a person who must be extracted, not a thing. |
| **5** | Inside job: a contact on the inside is already in motion, and their plan is incompatible with yours. |
| **6** | Sealed environment: the vault is in vacuum, on a hostile world, or in substrate-adjacent space. |
| **7** | Witness: the asset's owner is present and unaware, and the crew must extract without their knowledge. |
| **8** | Misidentified asset: the real target is not the obvious target; the obvious target is a decoy. |
| **9** | Double-blind: the client knows about the counter-team and is using the crew as a distraction. |
| **10** | Cleanup contract: the heist is to *return* something previously stolen, and the current owner is the original thief. |


### SABOTAGE SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS SABOTAGE DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The target must continue functioning until a specific moment, then fail. |
| **2** | The target must fail in a way that cannot be traced to deliberate action. |
| **3** | The target's failure must implicate a specific third party. |
| **4** | The target has redundant systems; all of them must be disabled. |
| **5** | The target is staffed by people the crew has no quarrel with. |
| **6** | A failure here will hurt civilians; the crew must minimize collateral. |
| **7** | The target is being protected by a security service whose presence is itself classified. |
| **8** | The target is one of multiple identical sites; the crew must be sure they have the right one. |
| **9** | The client's stated reason for the sabotage is a lie; the real reason matters. |
| **10** | The sabotage will create a problem the client expects the crew to solve next. |


### SALVAGE SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS SALVAGE DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The wreck is haunted: substrate phenomena have made the site psychologically dangerous. |
| **2** | The wreck is contested: other salvagers are already on-site or en route. |
| **3** | The wreck is not abandoned: someone or something still lives there. |
| **4** | The wreck contains Precursor material; Imperial Custody is en route. |
| **5** | The wreck's hull is structurally unstable and will collapse within the operation window. |
| **6** | The wreck is in a jurisdiction where salvage is restricted by treaty. |
| **7** | The wreck is the burial site for a culture that considers disturbance a desecration. |
| **8** | The wreck contains evidence of a crime the salvagers do not want to investigate but will. |
| **9** | The wreck's previous occupants did not all leave; some are in stasis. |
| **10** | The wreck is a trap; the salvage opportunity was bait. |


### RESCUE SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS RESCUE DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The hostage does not want to be rescued. |
| **2** | The hostage is being held by people who do not know they are holding a hostage. |
| **3** | The hostage's location is unknown; the rescue starts with intelligence work. |
| **4** | The hostage has been there long enough to have stockholm-bonded with the captors. |
| **5** | The hostage has been replaced; the captors are still holding a person, but it is not the one the client paid for. |
| **6** | The hostage is in a different jurisdiction; the rescue is also a smuggling operation. |
| **7** | The hostage's captor is a former ally of one crew member. |
| **8** | The hostage is being kept alive by a system that cannot be moved; rescue requires extracting both. |
| **9** | The hostage was taken by mistake; the captors think they have someone else. |
| **10** | The hostage is a child, and the client is not a parent. |


### INVESTIGATION SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS INVESTIGATION DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The trail is cold; physical evidence has degraded. |
| **2** | The witnesses are hostile to the crew's species or faction. |
| **3** | The case has been investigated before; previous investigators are dead, missing, or compromised. |
| **4** | The client is implicated by the evidence and does not yet know. |
| **5** | The answer is not what anyone wants to hear. |
| **6** | The investigation is being shadowed by another investigator who is not introducing themselves. |
| **7** | Crucial evidence has been classified; accessing it requires breaking secondary laws. |
| **8** | A witness offers to confess, but to a different crime than the one being investigated. |
| **9** | The crime has not yet happened; the client wants prevention, not punishment. |
| **10** | The crime has happened many times; the crew is not the first to be hired. |


### SMUGGLING SPECIFICS (D10)


| D10 | WHAT MAKES THIS RUN DIFFERENT |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | The cargo is sentient and has opinions. |
| **2** | The cargo's owner will not say what it is. |
| **3** | The cargo's owner will not say *why* it is being moved. |
| **4** | The route is being watched; the crew was selected because they have not yet been associated with the route. |
| **5** | The destination contact is dead, replaced, or compromised. |
| **6** | A second smuggler is using the same route at the same time, unaware. |
| **7** | The cargo's value is not in the contraband but in something hidden inside it. |
| **8** | The crew is being tracked by their own client to verify route security. |
| **9** | A piece of the cargo is missing at pickup; the seller will not acknowledge it. |
| **10** | The cargo includes a passenger nobody told the crew about. |


## 21.7: MISSION LENGTH CALIBRATION


A mission can be sized to fit the session window. Use the following calibrations:


| TARGET LENGTH | BEATS | MISSION SHAPE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1-2 hours** | 3-4 | One location, one objective, one twist. Resolve in scenes, not arcs. |
| **3-4 hours** | 5-6 | Two-three locations, primary + secondary objective, one twist with consequence. |
| **5-6 hours (one-shot)** | 7-9 | Full Client + Job + Twist + Specialty cycle. Multiple stakeholders. |
| **Multi-session (2-3)** | 10-15 | The single mission becomes an arc. Twist reveals deeper twist. Original client may not be the final client. |
| **Campaign mission (4+)** | open | The job becomes the campaign. Resolution opens new questions. |


For short sessions, *cut twists*. For long campaigns, *layer them*. The framework scales; the table sets the duration by deciding which beats matter.

# CHAPTER 22: QUICK REFERENCE & APPENDICES

> **Reference authority:** This appendix summarizes equipment statistics and Feature definitions. If a summary conflicts with a complete entry in the main chapters, the complete entry controls.

## CORE RESOLUTION REFERENCE

- Difficulty Classes: 5 Routine, 10 Easy, 15 Challenging, 20 Difficult, 25 Extreme, 30 Nearly Impossible.
- Traits modify attack rolls, not damage.
- Multi-die weapons apply Proficiency to one listed die only.
- Player criticals double the normal damage dice.
- Keeper criticals use maximum normal damage and resolve against thresholds and Armor Slots normally.
- Armor Slots recover through the Repair Armor Short Rest move or Repair All Armor Long Rest move.
- The Corebook remains authoritative. Optional alternatives in this supplement apply only when explicitly adopted by the table.

# CHAPTER 23: OPTIONAL RULES & CRUNCH TIERS

> **OPTIONAL RULES:** Nothing in this chapter replaces the Corebook unless the table explicitly adopts the named option before play. Record adopted options in the campaign notes.

*Player-facing guidance for choosing the expansion modules that suit the table.*

Rust & Steel is modular. Use an entire subsystem, its simplified alternative, or neither. Complexity is useful only when it creates decisions the group enjoys.

## THE CRUNCH SCALE

| RATING | LABEL | DESCRIPTION |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Minimal | Reference or fiction with almost no tracking. |
| 2 | Light | One small track, choice, or recurring number. |
| 3 | Moderate | A regular procedure with interacting choices. |
| 4 | Heavy | A dedicated subsystem with persistent state. |
| 5 | Complex | Several linked subsystems with campaign-level state. |

Higher crunch is not better or worse. It measures table overhead.
